# Getting started

`@deltabox/toolchain` is a config-driven layer around [Vite+](https://viteplus.dev).
It exists to remove the glue work that appears once a project grows beyond a
single package: the same settings spread across a dozen files, generated files
that drift, and release chores that are easy to get wrong.

You describe the project once, and the toolchain keeps the rest in sync.

## Install

::: code-group

```sh [npm]
# as a dev dependency in the project you want to manage
npm install @deltabox/toolchain --save-dev
```

```sh [yarn]
# as a dev dependency in the project you want to manage
yarn add -D @deltabox/toolchain
```

```sh [pnpm]
# as a dev dependency in the project you want to manage
pnpm add -D @deltabox/toolchain
```

```sh [bun]
# as a dev dependency in the project you want to manage
bun add -D @deltabox/toolchain
```

:::

```sh
# or for global usage
npm install -g @deltabox/toolchain
```

The published package exposes one binary, `dbx`:

```sh
dbx --help
```

## Interactive CLI

Commands are flag-driven, but in an interactive terminal (a TTY) a few prompt for
the values you omit:

```sh
dbx create                     # pick a template, project name, scope, inputs and actions
dbx migrate --recursive        # pick which projects to migrate
```

`dbx migrate` without `--from` still detects the sources automatically; the
prompt is only for the project selection with `--recursive`. Pass `--json`, pipe
the command, or supply the flags to run non-interactively. `dbx template:init`
also accepts flags (`--name`, `--kind`, ...) for scripted use.

## Create a config

Add the `dbx()` plugin to `vite.config.ts` (recommended, no `dbx.config.*` needed):

```ts
import { dbx } from '@deltabox/toolchain/vite';

export default {
    plugins: [dbx({ toolchain: { fmt: true, lint: true } })],
};
```

See [Vite plugin](/guide/vite-plugin) for the install steps and what the plugin
does.

Or, for a project that does not use Vite, scaffold a standalone config:

```sh
dbx project:config        # detect + write dbx.config.ts
```

Or start from a template:

```sh
dbx template:list
dbx create --template project --name my-app --out ./my-app
```

## Sync

`sync` runs every enabled task and writes the managed files (adding a manifest at
`.dbx/toolchain/manifest.json`):

```sh
dbx sync              # write managed files
dbx sync --check      # CI: fail if files are out of date
dbx sync --recursive  # every managed project, in dependency order
dbx sync --only tsconfig  # only refresh tsconfig aliases/references
dbx watch             # re-sync on change
```

The generated state lives under `.dbx/`. Add it to `.gitignore`, keeping only
the manifest (it holds no absolute paths):

```gitignore
.dbx/*
!.dbx/toolchain
.dbx/toolchain/*
!.dbx/toolchain/manifest.json
```

`dbx sync` adds this block to an existing `.gitignore` automatically, so you only
need to add it by hand when the repo has no `.gitignore` yet.

## What gets managed

| Area                                                                | Section in the config         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| GitHub workflows, commitlint, Conventional-Commits VS Code settings | `ci`                          |
| `biome.json` (formatter/linter)                                     | `fmt.biome` / `lint.biome`    |
| `.oxfmtrc.json` / `.oxlintrc.json` (Oxc)                            | `fmt.oxc` / `lint.oxc`        |
| Workspace `tsconfig.json` files (aliases + references)              | `tsconfig`                    |
| `vite.config.ts` (Vite+ consumers)                                  | `vite`                        |
| Template sources / scaffolding                                      | `templates`                   |
| Package catalogs (`.yarnrc.yml` / `pnpm-workspace.yaml`)            | [`catalogs`](/guide/catalogs) |
| Watch behaviour                                                     | `watch`                       |

Every section is **opt-in by presence**: define it to enable it, omit it to leave
that area untouched.

# Why use this?

`@deltabox/toolchain` is a config-driven layer around [Vite+](https://viteplus.dev).
It exists to remove the glue work that appears once a project grows beyond a
single package: the same settings spread across a dozen files, generated files
that drift, and release chores that are easy to get wrong.

You describe the project once, and the toolchain keeps the rest in sync.

The open-source [`dbx` toolchain repository](https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain)
uses the toolchain itself to maintain its development: sync, config generation,
`tsconfig` management, changelog/release automation and the docs site are all
driven by the same setup described here. That dogfooding keeps the workflow
honest.

## The problems it removes

### Configuration sprawl

A typical TypeScript project ends up with separate configs for Vite, Vitest,
TypeScript, formatting, linting, CI, changelog automation, editor settings and
Docker. They overlap, disagree, and are updated at different times.

With dbx, those settings live in one `dbx.config.*` (or inline in the `dbx()`
Vite plugin). Each section is opt-in, so you only own the parts you use.

### Monorepo drift

Hand-maintained `tsconfig` references, path aliases, workspace dependency
ranges, catalogs, scripts and managed files are routine sources of breakage.
One package gets a new alias, another keeps an old `tsconfig`, CI starts
failing.

The project graph, `tsconfig` generation and `dbx sync --check` keep those
artifacts consistent and make drift visible before it lands.

### Local and CI differences

"Works on my machine" usually means a different formatter version, a missing
commit hook, stale generated files or a release step that only runs locally.

The toolchain uses it's commands in generated files and hooks locally
and in CI, with `sync --check` as a single verification gate.
For Vite+ projects it passes through Vite+ commands.

### Release and CI glue

Changelog formatting, version bumps, release notes, issue and PR links,
Dependabot updates and workflow maintenance are recurring work that has little
to do with the product.

dbx generates the workflows and the changelog pipeline from the same config, so
releases stay repeatable and the release notes stay readable.

### Inconsistent scaffolding

Every new package starts from a different copy of "the right setup", and the
copy slowly diverges.

Builtin templates and generators produce a consistent project shape, including
Vite+, Oxc, `tsconfig`, CI, catalogs and Docker when requested.

### Toolchain version skew

Keeping `vite`, `vitest`, `tsdown`, Oxfmt and Oxlint aligned across a repo is
its own maintenance task. Vite+ already bundles them; dbx leans on that single
toolchain instead of installing each tool separately.

## What you get

* **One config, opt-in sections.** `project`, `ci`, `tsconfig`, `templates`,
  `fmt`/`lint`, `vite`, `watch`, `logger`, `providers` and more.
* **Sync with drift detection.** `dbx sync` writes managed files; `dbx sync --check` fails when they are stale.
* **A Vite+ integration.** The `dbx()` plugin carries the config inline and
  adds fmt/lint, tasks, hooks and passthrough commands.
* **A config generator.** Turn schemas into env docs, TypeScript types, JSON
  Schema and typed CLI options.
* **Project-aware tooling.** Workspace graph, tsconfig refs/aliases, catalogs
  and per-package releases.
* **Scaffolds and templates.** Consistent projects, workspaces, built-in & custom
  libraries, server templates and Vite apps.
* **Automated maintenance.** CI, changelog, releases, issues and Dependabot
  workflows.
* **Editor and agent integration.** A VS Code extension and an MCP server for
  the same APIs.

## Core features

### VS Code extension

The extension turns the same project model into a UI: browse managed files and
the project graph, run sync and migrations, scaffold projects, open provider
commands and inspect what the toolchain manages. It reads provider and project
data from the CLI, so it stays aligned with the terminal workflow instead of
being a separate configuration surface. See the
[VS Code extension guide](/guide/vscode).

### Config generator and engine

The config engine is a schema-first way to describe configuration once and
derive the surrounding artifacts from it. It generates TypeScript types, env
docs, JSON Schema and typed CLI options/programs, and provides file/env/CLI
loaders with predictable precedence. Teams that ship a config format can reuse
that machinery instead of hand-writing each output. See the
[Config generator guide](/guide/config-generator/).

### Providers

Providers describe the external toolchains a project can use, starting with
Vite+. The CLI and the VS Code extension consume the same provider descriptors,
so commands, availability and metadata do not drift between the terminal and
the editor.

Providers are not limited to JavaScript. A descriptor can wrap any CLI binary,
so the same surface can expose Python (`uv`, `ruff`, `pytest`), C#/.NET
(`dotnet`), Java (Maven or Gradle), Rust (`cargo`), Go and other language
toolchains. A polyglot repo can use `dbx python:*`, `dbx rust:*`, `dbx dotnet:*`
and the rest without teaching the terminal, CI and editor a different command
set for every language. See [Providers](/guide/providers#other-language-toolchains).

### MCP

The MCP server exposes the public toolchain APIs to AI agents and editors. You
can install it for Claude, Codex, VS Code, OpenCode, Pi or a custom directory,
then let an agent inspect projects, configs and generated files through the same
commands and types a developer uses. See [MCP](/guide/mcp).

## Who it is for

It is most useful when at least one of these is true:

* you **maintain a monorepo** or several related packages;
* you want **one place** for **toolchain, CI and release configuration**;
* you use **Vite or Vite+** and want a **consistent project workflow**;
* you define **schemas or config formats** and want **types, docs, JSON Schema
  and typed CLI options** generated from them;
* you maintain **many environment variables** and want **documented, typed
  config** with **file/env/CLI precedence**;
* you want **one consistent CLI and task surface** for scripts, tasks and
  provider toolchains;
* you build a **library or internal tool** that needs its own **typed config and
  CLI** without rebuilding loaders, validation and help;
* you work **across languages** and want Python, .NET, Java, Rust and other
  tools exposed through the **same command surface**;
* you **scaffold projects or packages** regularly;
* you work in **VS Code or with AI agents** and want them to understand the
  **same project model**;
* you are tired of **generated files and release chores drifting**.

## When it might not fit

A tiny single-file project rarely needs the full surface. A team with a very
bespoke pipeline may prefer to keep it in-house. Because every section is
opt-in, you can also start with only `project` and `tsconfig`, then add
automation later.

The toolchain is a dev dependency. It does not replace Vite+ at runtime; it
makes the project around Vite+ easier to keep consistent.

## Where to go next

* [Getting started](/guide/) — install the CLI and create a config.
* [Monorepo guide](/guide/monorepo) — project graph, `tsconfig` and tasks.
* [Vite+](/guide/vite) — plugin mode, config mode and local CLI usage.
* [Package scripts](/guide/scripts) — the recommended `fmt`, `check`, `test`
  and `sync` scripts.

# Overview

There are four ways to configure dbx. They all feed the same toolchain
model, so a project can combine them.

## `dbx.config.*`

A standalone config file (`dbx.config.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.js`, `.mjs`,
`.cjs` or `.json`) exports `{ toolchain: { ... } }` with `defineConfig`.

It is the non-Vite path and is typed as `ToolchainConfig` (see the
[TypeScript guide](/guide/typescript)). Every section is opt-in by presence.

## Vite plugin

In a Vite or Vite+ project, pass the same `toolchain` object to the `dbx()`
plugin in `vite.config.*`.

The CLI reads it back from the Vite config, so no
`dbx.config.*` is required. See [Vite plugin](/guide/vite-plugin).

## CLI

`dbx` command flags configure a command for one run. The available options are
generated from the command descriptors. See the [CLI reference](/config/cli).

## Environment variables

Schema leaves that declare `.meta({ envName })` can be set through env vars (the
toolchain config uses the `DBX_` prefix).

See the [environment reference](/config/env) and the
[Config Generator](/guide/config-generator/).

## Editor JSON Schema

The generated [config.schema.json](https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/config.schema.json)
gives editors completion and validation for `dbx.config.*`.

The exhaustive object reference is [dbx.config](/config/reference).

## Types

Find all static types for the configurations
[here](https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/blob/main/packages/shared/src/config-types.ts).

### Fields

Every generated config reference page uses the same
[ConfigMeta](https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/blob/main/packages/config/src/types/meta.ts)
fields defined in Zod/Untyped schemas:

* `description`
* `required`
* `deprecated`
* `example`
* `secret`
* `scope`
* `public`
* `defaultValue`
* `envName` (the env fields)
* `envPath`
* `cli` / `cliCommand` (schema-driven CLI flags and commands)
* `envExpose` (keep a value CLI-only) and more.

# CLI reference

Generated from the same `CliCommand` descriptors the `dbx` binary registers.

| Command                                                 | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`dbx projects`](#projects)                             | Discover projects and write .dbx/toolchain/projects.json.                                       |
| [`dbx sync`](#sync)                                     | Regenerate every managed file from dbx.config.*.                                                |
| [`dbx watch`](#watch)                                   | Sync once, then watch key files and re-sync on change.                                          |
| [`dbx reset`](#reset)                                   | Remove generated files, the .dbx/toolchain manifest and/or the dbx config from a project.       |
| [`dbx providers`](#providers)                           | List the tooling providers (Vite+, ...) and their commands.                                     |
| [`dbx enabled`](#enabled)                               | Print whether the toolchain is enabled for this project (and the scope).                        |
| [`dbx enable`](#enable)                                 | Enable the toolchain (workspace scope by default).                                              |
| [`dbx disable`](#disable)                               | Disable the toolchain (workspace scope by default).                                             |
| [`dbx tsconfig`](#tsconfig)                             | Generate workspace tsconfig.json files from the default tsconfig (aliases + references).        |
| [`dbx cleanup`](#cleanup)                               | Remove build artifacts (*.tsbuildinfo, dist/).                                                  |
| [`dbx cleanup:turbo`](#cleanup-turbo)                   | Remove the turbo cache (.turbo/).                                                               |
| [`dbx workflow`](#workflow)                             | Trigger generated workflows with their vendor CLI (`gh`, `glab` or `az`).                       |
| [`dbx changelog`](#changelog)                           | Scan commits, derive the semver bump and update the CHANGELOG.md files + versions.              |
| [`dbx mcp:serve`](#mcp-serve)                           | Run the dbx MCP server over stdio (for MCP clients).                                            |
| [`dbx mcp:install`](#mcp-install)                       | Install the dbx MCP server + skill into an AI harness/editor.                                   |
| [`dbx mcp:list`](#mcp-list)                             | List the builtin MCP providers (Claude, Codex, VS Code, OpenCode, Pi).                          |
| [`dbx migrate`](#migrate)                               | Migrate Biome / ESLint / Prettier / Dprint / Oxc config, or fold vite.config.\* into dbx.config. |
| [`dbx migrate:list`](#migrate-list)                     | List the registered migrations and whether each is detected.                                    |
| [`dbx project:init`](#project-init)                     | Scaffold a single-package TypeScript project.                                                   |
| [`dbx project:init:monorepo`](#project-init-monorepo)   | Scaffold a monorepo root (add --example for one example workspace).                             |
| [`dbx project:init:workspace`](#project-init-workspace) | Scaffold a monorepo workspace package into an existing monorepo root.                           |
| [`dbx project:config`](#project-config)                 | Generate dbx.config.\* for existing projects that are missing one.                               |
| [`dbx template:list`](#template-list)                   | List templates (builtin + local + opted-in online sources).                                     |
| [`dbx template:init`](#template-init)                   | Write a template.json to a directory, making it a local template.                               |
| [`dbx template:add`](#template-add)                     | Record a template source in .dbx/toolchain/templates.json.                                      |
| [`dbx template:remove`](#template-remove)               | Remove a source from .dbx/toolchain/templates.json.                                             |
| [`dbx template:registry`](#template-registry)           | Manage the global template search paths (and sync them to the VS Code setting).                 |
| [`dbx registry`](#registry)                             | List or manage the template/provider registries.                                                |
| [`dbx template:info`](#template-info)                   | Show one template by id.                                                                        |
| [`dbx create`](#create)                                 | Scaffold a project from a template (builtin, local or Vite+).                                   |
| [`dbx vite`](#vite)                                     | Run any Vite+ command through `vp` (eg. `dbx vite dev`).                                        |
| [`dbx vite:create`](#vite-create)                       | Vite+: Create a new project from a template.                                                    |
| [`dbx vite:migrate`](#vite-migrate)                     | Vite+: Migrate an existing project to Vite+.                                                    |
| [`dbx vite:config`](#vite-config)                       | Vite+: Configure hooks and agent integration.                                                   |
| [`dbx vite:hooks`](#vite-hooks)                         | Vite+: Manage the Git hook dispatcher.                                                          |
| [`dbx vite:staged`](#vite-staged)                       | Vite+: Run linters on staged files.                                                             |
| [`dbx vite:install`](#vite-install)                     | Vite+: Install dependencies with the detected package manager.                                  |
| [`dbx vite:env`](#vite-env)                             | Vite+: Manage Node.js and package managers.                                                     |
| [`dbx vite:dev`](#vite-dev)                             | Vite+: Run the Vite development server.                                                         |
| [`dbx vite:check`](#vite-check)                         | Vite+: Run format, lint and type checks.                                                        |
| [`dbx vite:lint`](#vite-lint)                           | Vite+: Lint code with the active linter (Oxlint via Vite+).                                     |
| [`dbx vite:fmt`](#vite-fmt)                             | Vite+: Format code with the active formatter (Oxfmt via Vite+).                                 |
| [`dbx vite:test`](#vite-test)                           | Vite+: Run tests through bundled Vitest.                                                        |
| [`dbx vite:run`](#vite-run)                             | Vite+: Run package scripts and monorepo tasks.                                                  |
| [`dbx vite:exec`](#vite-exec)                           | Vite+: Execute a binary from local node_modules.                                                |
| [`dbx vite:node`](#vite-node)                           | Vite+: Run a Node.js script in the Vite+ env.                                                   |
| [`dbx vite:dlx`](#vite-dlx)                             | Vite+: Run a package binary without installing it.                                              |
| [`dbx vite:cache`](#vite-cache)                         | Vite+: Manage the task cache.                                                                   |
| [`dbx vite:build`](#vite-build)                         | Vite+: Build for production.                                                                    |
| [`dbx vite:pack`](#vite-pack)                           | Vite+: Build libraries for npm or standalone binaries.                                          |
| [`dbx vite:preview`](#vite-preview)                     | Vite+: Preview the production build.                                                            |
| [`dbx vite:add`](#vite-add)                             | Vite+: Add packages to dependencies.                                                            |
| [`dbx vite:remove`](#vite-remove)                       | Vite+: Remove packages from dependencies.                                                       |
| [`dbx vite:update`](#vite-update)                       | Vite+: Update packages.                                                                         |
| [`dbx vite:dedupe`](#vite-dedupe)                       | Vite+: Deduplicate dependencies.                                                                |
| [`dbx vite:outdated`](#vite-outdated)                   | Vite+: Check for outdated packages.                                                             |
| [`dbx vite:list`](#vite-list)                           | Vite+: List installed packages.                                                                 |
| [`dbx vite:why`](#vite-why)                             | Vite+: Explain why a package is installed.                                                      |
| [`dbx vite:info`](#vite-info)                           | Vite+: View package metadata.                                                                   |
| [`dbx vite:link`](#vite-link)                           | Vite+: Link local packages.                                                                     |
| [`dbx vite:unlink`](#vite-unlink)                       | Vite+: Unlink local packages.                                                                   |
| [`dbx vite:rebuild`](#vite-rebuild)                     | Vite+: Rebuild native modules.                                                                  |
| [`dbx vite:pm`](#vite-pm)                               | Vite+: Forward a command to the package manager.                                                |
| [`dbx vite:toolchain`](#vite-toolchain)                 | Vite+: Show Vite+ tool versions.                                                                |
| [`dbx vite:upgrade`](#vite-upgrade)                     | Vite+: Update `vp` itself.                                                                      |
| [`dbx vite:implode`](#vite-implode)                     | Vite+: Remove `vp` and all related data.                                                        |
| [`dbx fmt`](#fmt)                                       | Format with the detected formatter (Vite+ Oxfmt, Prettier, Biome, dprint or Oxc).               |
| [`dbx lint`](#lint)                                     | Lint with the detected linter (Vite+ Oxlint, ESLint or Biome).                                  |

## `dbx projects`

Discover projects and write .dbx/toolchain/projects.json.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Root to scan (default: cwd).
* `--max-depth ‹n›` — Max directory depth. (default: `5`)
* `--no-write` — Do not write the graph file.
* `--json` — Print the graph as JSON.

## `dbx sync`

Regenerate every managed file from dbx.config.\*.

* `--no-format` — Do not format the written managed files.
* `--no-format-fix` — Run the formatter in check mode instead of rewriting the files.
* `--format-command ‹value›` — Override the formatter command. `{files}` expands to the managed files (space-separated); when it is absent the files are appended.
* `--format-exclude ‹value...›` — Globs of managed files to leave unformatted (per-file opt-out).
* `--check` — Do not write; fail if files are out of date.
* `--watch` — Keep running and re-sync on change.
* `--recursive` — Sync every managed project in dependency order (nested workspaces included; configless projects only with --configless).
* `--force` — Run even when no dbx.config.\* is present.
* `--only ‹tasks›` — Only run the named sync task(s), comma-separated (eg. `tsconfig`).
* `--json` — Print the sync result (including removed files) as JSON.

## `dbx watch`

Sync once, then watch key files and re-sync on change.

* `--debounce ‹value›` — Debounce window in ms. (default: `150`)
* `--exclude ‹value...›` — Glob(s) excluded from watching. Defaults to the common ignored paths (`node_modules`, `.dbx`, `dist`, `build`, ...).
* `--no-gitignore` — Do not respect .gitignore files.
* `--force` — Run even when no dbx.config.\* is present.
* `--list` — Print the resolved input globs (+ tsconfig file names) instead of watching.
* `--json` — With --list: print the inputs as JSON.

## `dbx reset`

Remove generated files, the .dbx/toolchain manifest and/or the dbx config from a project.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--recursive` — Reset every discovered project under the root.
* `--include ‹pattern...›` —
* `--exclude ‹pattern...›` —
* `--generated` — Remove only the generated/managed files.
* `--manifest` — Remove only the .dbx/toolchain directory.
* `--config` — Also remove dbx.config.\*.
* `--all` — Remove generated files, the manifest and the config.
* `--dry-run` — Report what would be removed without deleting.
* `--json` — Print the result as JSON.

## `dbx providers`

List the tooling providers (Vite+, ...) and their commands.

* `--json` — Print the providers (with actions) as JSON.

## `dbx enabled`

Print whether the toolchain is enabled for this project (and the scope).

* `--json` — Print the resolved state as JSON.

## `dbx enable`

Enable the toolchain (workspace scope by default).

* `--global` — Set the global scope (`~/.dbx/toolchain/cli/config.json`).
* `--workspace` — Set the workspace scope (`.vscode/settings.json`).
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--json` — Print the result as JSON.

## `dbx disable`

Disable the toolchain (workspace scope by default).

* `--global` — Set the global scope (`~/.dbx/toolchain/cli/config.json`).
* `--workspace` — Set the workspace scope (`.vscode/settings.json`).
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--json` — Print the result as JSON.

## `dbx tsconfig`

Generate workspace tsconfig.json files from the default tsconfig (aliases + references).

* `--glob ‹value...›` — Glob(s) for the workspace default tsconfig files. Defaults to matching every `defaultFile` recursively.
* `--exclude ‹value...›` — Glob(s) to exclude from `glob`. Defaults to the common ignored paths (`node_modules`, `.dbx`, `dist`, `build`, ...).
* `--no-gitignore` — Do not respect .gitignore files.
* `--refs` — Wire project references.
* `--composite` — Emit `composite: true`.
* `--no-aliases` — Skip path aliases.
* `--flatten-remote-extends` — Inline the compiler options inherited from a remote `http(s)` `extends` chain into the generated workspace configs. Useful when a tool cannot follow a remote URL; path-valued options such as `paths`/`baseUrl` are skipped because they describe the remote tree. Settings the generated config already defines always win.
* `--auto-src-dir ‹value›` — Source directory used to resolve workspace entry points when `package.json` does not declare `exports`/`main`/`types` (default: the workspace's final tsconfig `rootDir`/`baseUrl`, falling back to `src`).
* `-i, --indent ‹value›` — JSON indentation. (default: `4`)
* `--root-file ‹value›` — The workspaces tsconfig file name that holds `paths` + `references`. (default: `tsconfig.workspaces.json`)
* `--default-file ‹value›` — The workspace default tsconfig file name that the generator expands. (default: `tsconfig.default.json`)
* `--build-file ‹value›` — The workspace build tsconfig file name. (default: `tsconfig.build.json`)
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Repo root to scan (default: cwd).
* `--auto` — Auto-wire the root workspaces tsconfig paths/references from the project graph (default false).
* `--no-auto` — Only use the paths/references already in the root workspaces tsconfig.
* `--auto-aliases` — Auto-wire path aliases (defaults to --auto).
* `--no-auto-aliases` — Do not auto-wire path aliases.
* `--auto-refs` — Auto-wire project references (defaults to --auto).
* `--no-auto-refs` — Do not auto-wire project references.
* `--tsconfig ‹file›` — Resolve this tsconfig instead of \<root>/tsconfig.json.
* `--root ‹dir›` — Root used to detect/resolve the tsconfig (default: cwd).
* `--json` — Print the resolved { alias, paths, references } object.
* `--alias` — Print only the resolved Vite/Vitest aliases.
* `--paths` — Print only the resolved compilerOptions.paths.
* `--references` — Print only the resolved project references.
* `--no-extends` — Do not follow the tsconfig extends chain.
* `--restore [kind]` — Remove the applied tsconfig overrides (all, or base|root|default|build) using the manifest snapshots.

## `dbx cleanup`

Remove build artifacts (\*.tsbuildinfo, dist/).

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Directory to clean (default: cwd).
* `--pattern ‹glob...›` — Override the match globs.

## `dbx cleanup:turbo`

Remove the turbo cache (.turbo/).

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Directory to clean (default: cwd).

## `dbx workflow`

Trigger generated workflows with their vendor CLI (`gh`, `glab` or `az`).

* `[workflows]` — Workflow ids, custom ids, or file names (default: every enabled workflow).
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--ref ‹ref›` — Git ref to run the workflow on.
* `--gh ‹cmd›` — The gh executable (default: gh).
* `--glab ‹cmd›` — The glab executable (default: glab).
* `--az ‹cmd›` — The az executable (default: az).
* `--list` — List the enabled workflows (and where they are written).
* `--json` — With --list: print the workflows as JSON.

## `dbx changelog`

Scan commits, derive the semver bump and update the CHANGELOG.md files + versions.

* `--range ‹range›` — Git revision range to scan.
* `--dry-run` — Print the proposed entry without writing.
* `--version ‹semver›` — Override the version.
* `--base-version ‹semver›` — Bump from this version instead.
* `--release-body ‹semver›` — Print the release body for this version and exit.
* `--release-group` — Group every version since the previous published release into the body.
* `--no-release-group` — Disable release grouping configured in the changelog config.
* `--release-since ‹version›` — Group from this version/tag instead of the released boundary.
* `--release-include-prereleases` — Let prerelease versions bound the grouped release body.
* `--processing-method ‹method›` — `latest` (default), `all`, or a git range.
* `--format-only` — Only regroup existing changelogs.
* `--release-body-wrap` — Wrap the generated entry as a `**Release notes**` details block.
* `--intro ‹text›` — Inline intro text for the new changelog entry.
* `--intro-file ‹file›` — Read the new entry intro text from a file.
* `--outro ‹text›` — Inline outro text for the new changelog entry.
* `--outro-file ‹file›` — Read the new entry outro text from a file.
* `--no-package-changes-section` — Skip the package-changes footer.

## `dbx mcp:serve`

Run the dbx MCP server over stdio (for MCP clients).

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).

## `dbx mcp:install`

Install the dbx MCP server + skill into an AI harness/editor.

* `--provider ‹id›` — claude, codex, vscode, opencode, pi or custom.
* `--scope ‹scope›` — project (default) or global.
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--dir ‹dir›` — Custom directory (for --provider custom).
* `--command ‹command›` — Client command (default `dbx`)
* `--no-skills` — Do not write the skill/instructions file.
* `--json` — Print the written paths as JSON.

## `dbx mcp:list`

List the builtin MCP providers (Claude, Codex, VS Code, OpenCode, Pi).

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--json` — Print the providers as JSON.

## `dbx migrate`

Migrate Biome / ESLint / Prettier / Dprint / Oxc config, or fold vite.config.\* into dbx.config.

* `--from ‹tool›` — Source tool (repeatable): biome | eslint | prettier | dprint | oxc | vite | all.
* `--to ‹tool›` — Target tool (default: oxc). (default: `oxc`)
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--recursive` — Also migrate the discovered projects under the root (default: root only).
* `--write` — Write the files (default: dry-run).
* `--dry-run` — Do not write anything (default).
* `--check` — CI: exit non-zero when the oxc config is stale.
* `--target ‹target›` — files (default) | vite.
* `--online` — Allow network (e.g. @oxlint/migrate).
* `--ignore-vite-config-file` — Do not remove the folded `vite.config.*`.
* `--ignore-managed-files` — Skip the post-migration sync (leave the toolchain-managed files as-is).
* `--ignore-changelog` — Skip the changelog task in the post-migration sync.
* `--tool-version ‹name@range›` — Override a provisioned formatter/linter dependency version (repeatable).
* `--json` — Print the result as JSON.

## `dbx migrate:list`

List the registered migrations and whether each is detected.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--json` — Print as JSON.

## `dbx project:init`

Scaffold a single-package TypeScript project.

* `-n, --name ‹name›` — Project name.
* `-s, --scope ‹scope›` — npm scope, eg. @org.
* `-o, --out ‹dir›` — Output directory (default: cwd).
* `--package-manager ‹pm›` — Package manager: yarn (default) | pnpm | npm | bun.
* `--tool-version ‹name@range›` — Override a formatter/linter dependency version, eg. `oxfmt@^0.80.0`.
* `--containerize` — Also generate Docker artifacts (Dockerfile + .dockerignore).
* `--no-project-config` — Skip the generated vite.config.ts file (the project config).
* `--type ‹type›` — Project type: project | monorepo-root | monorepo-workspace.
* `--force` — Overwrite existing files in the output directory.

## `dbx project:init:monorepo`

Scaffold a monorepo root (add --example for one example workspace).

* `-n, --name ‹name›` — Project name.
* `-s, --scope ‹scope›` — npm scope, eg. @org.
* `-o, --out ‹dir›` — Output directory (default: cwd).
* `--example` — Also scaffold one example workspace package.
* `--package-manager ‹pm›` — Package manager: yarn (default) | pnpm | npm | bun.
* `--tool-version ‹name@range›` — Override a formatter/linter dependency version, eg. `oxfmt@^0.80.0`.
* `--no-project-config` — Skip the generated vite.config.ts file (the project config).
* `--type ‹type›` — Project type: project | monorepo-root | monorepo-workspace.
* `--force` — Overwrite existing files in the output directory.

## `dbx project:init:workspace`

Scaffold a monorepo workspace package into an existing monorepo root.

* `-n, --name ‹name›` — Workspace package name (unscoped).
* `-s, --scope ‹scope›` — npm scope, eg. @org.
* `-r, --root ‹dir›` — Monorepo root (default: cwd).
* `-d, --dir ‹dir›` — Workspace dir relative to the root (default: packages/\<name>).
* `--package-manager ‹pm›` — Package manager: yarn (default) | pnpm | npm | bun.
* `--tool-version ‹name@range›` — Override a formatter/linter dependency version, eg. `oxfmt@^0.80.0`.
* `--no-project-config` — Skip the generated vite.config.ts file (the project config).
* `--type ‹type›` — Project type: project | monorepo-root | monorepo-workspace.
* `--force` — Overwrite existing files in the output directory.

## `dbx project:config`

Generate dbx.config.\* for existing projects that are missing one.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Root to scan (default: cwd).
* `--include ‹pattern...›` — Only projects matching these patterns (glob or substring).
* `--exclude ‹pattern...›` — Skip projects matching these patterns (glob or substring).
* `--type ‹type›` — Force a project type for every config.
* `--language ‹language›` — Config language: ts (default) | js.
* `--config-extension ‹ext›` — Config extension: ts | mts | js | mjs | cjs (default inferred from the language and package type).
* `--skip-config` — Only write .dbx/toolchain/projects.json; do not create dbx.config.\* files.
* `--force` — Overwrite configs that already exist.
* `--dry-run` — Report what would be written without writing.
* `--json` — Print the result as JSON.

## `dbx template:list`

List templates (builtin + local + opted-in online sources).

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--online` — Resolve online sources (npm/git).
* `--offline` — Force offline (skip npm/git).
* `--global` — Only the global registry templates.
* `--kind ‹kind›` — project | workspace | application | folder | tooling | pipeline.
* `--registry` — List only the .dbx/toolchain/templates.json sources.
* `--json` — Print the templates as JSON.

## `dbx template:init`

Write a template.json to a directory, making it a local template.

* `[dir]` — Directory (default: cwd).
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--kind ‹kind›` — project | workspace | application | folder | tooling | pipeline.
* `--name ‹name›` — Display name (default: folder name).
* `--id ‹id›` — Stable template id (default: folder name).
* `--description ‹text›` — Description.
* `--var ‹pair...›` — Variable name\[:default] (repeatable).
* `--tag ‹tag...›` — Tag (repeatable).
* `--force` — Overwrite an existing template.json.
* `--add` — Also record the folder in .dbx/toolchain/templates.json.
* `--no-global` — Do not also store the template in the global registry.
* `--json` — Print the manifest as JSON.

## `dbx template:add`

Record a template source in .dbx/toolchain/templates.json.

* `‹source›` — local path | git URL | @scope/create | type:locate
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--type ‹type›` — Force: builtin | local | npm | git | vite-plus | remote.
* `--name ‹name›` — Display name.
* `--id ‹id›` — Stable template id (default: inferred).
* `--kind ‹kind›` — project | workspace | application | folder | tooling | pipeline.
* `--ref ‹ref›` — Git branch/tag/commit.
* `--registry ‹url›` — Custom npm registry (default: the project package manager).
* `--subdir ‹dir›` — Subdirectory within the source.
* `--no-global` — Do not also register the source in the global registry.
* `--json` — Print the updated registry as JSON.

## `dbx template:remove`

Remove a source from .dbx/toolchain/templates.json.

* `‹id›` — Source id or type:locate.
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--global` — Remove the template from the global registry.
* `--json` — Print the registry as JSON.

## `dbx template:registry`

Manage the global template search paths (and sync them to the VS Code setting).

* `--list` — List the resolved search paths (default).
* `--add ‹path...›` — Add global search path(s).
* `--remove ‹path...›` — Remove global search path(s).
* `--set ‹path...›` — Replace the global search paths.
* `--clear` — Reset the global search paths to the default.
* `--vscode-dir ‹dir›` — Record the VS Code user dir (its settings.json holds the paths).
* `--json` — Print the resolved config as JSON.

## `dbx registry`

List or manage the template/provider registries.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--kind ‹kind›` — What --add/--remove manages: templates | providers.
* `--add ‹path›` — Add a registry path (or remote URL).
* `--remove ‹path›` — Remove a registry path.
* `--set ‹path...›` — Replace the registry search paths.
* `--clear` — Clear the registry search paths.
* `--scope ‹scope›` — project | global (default: global).
* `--json` — Print the registries as JSON.

## `dbx template:info`

Show one template by id.

* `‹id›` — The template id.
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--online` — Resolve online sources.
* `--json` — Print the template as JSON (the default).

## `dbx create`

Scaffold a project from a template (builtin, local or Vite+).

* `-t, --template ‹id›` — Template id (see template:list).
* `--kind ‹kind›` — project | workspace | application | folder | tooling | pipeline.
* `-n, --name ‹name›` — Project / package name.
* `-s, --scope ‹scope›` — npm scope, eg. @org.
* `-o, --out ‹dir›` — Output directory (default: cwd).
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--var ‹pair...›` — Template variables as key=value (repeatable).
* `--action ‹id...›` — Action id to run after scaffolding (repeatable).
* `--tool-version ‹name@range›` — Override a provisioned formatter/linter dependency version (repeatable).
* `--online` — Resolve online templates too.
* `--force` — Overwrite existing files in the output directory.
* `--containerize` — Also generate Docker artifacts (Dockerfile + .dockerignore).
* `--json` — Print the result as JSON.

# Environment variables

The toolchain config is file/CLI backed; a schema leaf opts into an
environment variable with `.meta({ envName: "..." })` (see the
[Config Generator](/guide/config-generator/describe-a-scope)).

| Variable                            | Scope     | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `DBX_PROJECT_REGENERATE`            | toolchain | —       | Regenerate this section's managed files during `dbx sync`. When false, existing files are left untouched and are neither written nor drift-checked.                                        |
| `DBX_PROJECT_NAME`                  | toolchain | —       | The unscoped project name (written as `&lt;scope&gt;/&lt;name&gt;`).                                                                                                                       |
| `DBX_PROJECT_SCOPE`                 | toolchain | —       | The npm scope, eg. `@org`.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `DBX_PROJECT_AUTHOR`                | toolchain | —       | Package author (`package.json` `author`).                                                                                                                                                  |
| `DBX_PROJECT_LICENSE`               | toolchain | —       | SPDX license id (`package.json` `license`).                                                                                                                                                |
| `DBX_PROJECT_HOMEPAGE`              | toolchain | —       | Project homepage (`package.json` `homepage`).                                                                                                                                              |
| `DBX_PROJECT_REPO`                  | toolchain | —       | Repository URL (`package.json` `repository`). For a workspace it also resolves to the workspace path (`repository.directory`).                                                             |
| `DBX_PROJECT_NODEVERSION`           | toolchain | —       | Node version for CI/templates, eg. `22` (not `package.json` `engines`).                                                                                                                    |
| `DBX_PROJECT_PACKAGEMANAGER`        | toolchain | `yarn`  | Package manager name, written as `&lt;name&gt;@&lt;version&gt;`.                                                                                                                           |
| `DBX_PROJECT_PACKAGEMANAGERVERSION` | toolchain | —       | Package manager version, eg. `4.17.1`.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `DBX_PROJECT_DESCRIPTION`           | toolchain | —       | One-line description (`package.json` `description`).                                                                                                                                       |
| `DBX_PROJECT_INHERIT`               | toolchain | `true`  | Inherit the parent project metadata. Set false to keep this project metadata independent of the root config (other sections still merge normally).                                         |
| `DBX_PROJECT_MANAGECONFIGLESS`      | toolchain | `false` | Manage projects that have no dbx.config.\* of their own by inheriting the nearest ancestor config. Disabled by default so configless projects are never touched unless explicitly opted in. |
| `DBX_CI`                            | toolchain | `{}`    | GitHub Actions workflows to generate (CI, release, issues, changelog, sync).                                                                                                               |
| `DBX_CHANGELOG`                     | toolchain | `{}`    | Manual changelog pipeline options for `dbx changelog`, the VS Code actions and the API. `ci.changelog` inherits these options.                                                             |
| `DBX_FMT`                           | toolchain | `{}`    | Formatter configuration: Oxc/Biome options, editor defaults and tools.                                                                                                                     |
| `DBX_LINT`                          | toolchain | `{}`    | Linter configuration: Oxc/Biome/ESLint options and editor defaults.                                                                                                                        |
| `DBX_BIOME`                         | toolchain | `{}`    | Biome config generation (for consumers that still want a `biome.json`).                                                                                                                    |
| `DBX_TSCONFIG`                      | toolchain | `{}`    | Workspace tsconfig generation (path aliases + project references).                                                                                                                         |
| `DBX_LOADER`                        | toolchain | `{}`    | How `dbx.config.*` files are imported (tsconfig discovery).                                                                                                                                |
| `DBX_TEMPLATES`                     | toolchain | `{}`    | Template sources / scaffolding.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `DBX_REGISTRY`                      | toolchain | `{}`    | Allow/deny host and path globs for template/provider registries.                                                                                                                           |
| `DBX_CATALOGS`                      | toolchain | `{}`    | Package catalogs written to the package manager catalog file (`catalog:`).                                                                                                                 |
| `DBX_VITE`                          | toolchain | `{}`    | The full Vite+ config; `dbx sync` writes the root `vite.config.ts` from it.                                                                                                                |
| `DBX_WATCH`                         | toolchain | `{}`    | Watch behaviour for `dbx watch`.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `DBX_SYNC`                          | toolchain | `{}`    | `dbx sync` behaviour (formatting of the generated managed files).                                                                                                                          |
| `DBX_LOGGER`                        | toolchain | `{}`    | Logging level, colours and prefix for toolchain output.                                                                                                                                    |
| `DBX_PROVIDERS`                     | toolchain | `{}`    | Provider command behaviour (eg. colour for the passthrough commands).                                                                                                                      |

---
