| Markdown page  | `engine.markdown.file.generate()` / `.write()`               | `generateMarkdownFile()`                                  |
| Formatting     | —                                                            | `formatGenerated()`                                       |

## Env file — `.env.example`

```ts
engine.env.write({ output: '.env.example' });
```

Standalone, with the common options:

```ts
import { generateEnvFile } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const content = generateEnvFile(schema, {
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    header: 'Copy to .env and fill the blanks.',
    scopes: ['server', 'cli'],
    exclude: ['MYAPP_INTERNAL_TOKEN'],
    values: { MYAPP_PORT: '8080' },
    extra: { MYAPP_FEATURE_FLAG: 'true' },
});
```

Options: `include`/`exclude` (env names), `values` (default overrides),
`scopes`, `bare`, `extra` (raw `NAME=value` lines), `header`, `scopeSeparator`.
Secrets are emitted commented out.

## Env types — `env.ts` + `dbx-env.d.ts`

```ts
engine.env.types.write({ outputDir: 'types' }); // types/env.ts, types/dbx-env.d.ts
```

```ts
import { generateConfigEnv } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const files = generateConfigEnv(schema, {
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    outputDir: 'types',
    envInterfaceName: 'AppEnv',
    viteEnvInterfaceName: 'AppViteEnv',
    importPath: './env.js',
    augmentVite: true,
    envComment: 'Runtime configuration.',
});
// files: { 'env.ts': '...', 'dbx-env.d.ts': '...' }
```

Options: `envFile`/`dtsFile` (file names), `header`, `envHeader`, `dtsHeader`,
`augmentVite` (a `declare module 'vite'` augmentation).

## Config types

```ts
engine.types.write({ outputDir: 'types' });
```

Standalone, with hand-written overrides and aliases:

```ts
import { generateConfigTypes } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const files = generateConfigTypes(schema, {
    baseGroup: 'base',
    outputDir: 'types',
    interfaceNames: { server: 'ServerConfig' },
    aliases: { server: 'export type ServerOptions = ServerConfig;' },
    imports: ["import type { FastifyServerOptions } from 'fastify';"],
    overrides: {
        ServerConfig: `export interface ServerConfig {
    host?: string;
    port?: number;
}`,
    },
    header: '// Generated — do not edit.',
    extension: 'ts',
    includeEnv: false,
});
```

Options: `interfaceNames` (per scope), `aliases` (per scope, appended),
`overrides` (full declaration text, keyed by type name), `imports` (emitted once
at the top), `extension`, `header`, and the `include*` annotation flags.
`baseGroup` accepts a string or an array of strings; multiple groups are merged
into the generated `...Base` interface in declaration order.

## Markdown

```ts
engine.markdown.write({ outputDir: 'docs/reference/configuration' });
```

```ts
import { generateConfigMarkdown } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const files = generateConfigMarkdown(schema, {
    baseGroup: 'base',
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    outputDir: 'docs/reference/configuration',
    title: 'Configuration',
    frontmatter: ctx => `title: ${ctx.options.title ?? 'Configuration'}`,
    combined: true, // one index.md instead of one file per scope
    includeEnv: false,
});
```

`frontmatter: false` omits the frontmatter, a string replaces the body, and a
callback builds it from the generator options. `combined: true` renders every
scope into one file. `cliScope`, `shortFlags` and `references` control the CLI
equivalents and footer links.

## JSON Schema

```ts
const doc = await engine.jsonSchema.generate();
await engine.jsonSchema.write({ output: 'config.schema.json' });
```

```ts
import { generateConfigJsonSchema, generateJsonSchemaFile } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const doc = await generateConfigJsonSchema(schema, {
    baseGroup: 'base',
    id: 'https://myapp.dev/schemas/config.json',
    title: 'Myapp configuration',
    description: 'Every env-backed setting.',
});
const path = await generateJsonSchemaFile(schema, { output: 'config.schema.json' });
```

Both functions are async. `generateConfigJsonSchema` returns the document;
`generateJsonSchemaFile` writes it and returns the path.

`preserveDefs: true` keeps Zod's document-level `$ref`/`$defs` graph instead of
inlining every scope (the `$defs` tables are hoisted to the document root).
`scopeDescriptions` adds a description to a generated scope property, and
`additionalProperties` sets the root constraint:

```ts
const doc = await engine.jsonSchema.generate({
    preserveDefs: true,
    additionalProperties: false,
    scopeDescriptions: { server: 'Server settings.' },
});
```

## Config metadata JSON

```ts
const metadata = engine.configJson.build();
fs.writeFileSync('config.json', `${JSON.stringify(metadata, null, 4)}\n`);
```

```ts
import { buildConfigJson } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const metadata = buildConfigJson(schema, {
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    comment: 'Generated from the config schemas.',
});
```

The document contains `$comment`, `version`, and `env[]` entries with the name,
path, scope, description, default, `required`, `secret` and `public` flags.
Secrets never include a default.

## CLI options

```ts
const defs = engine.cli.generate({ scope: 'cli' });
```

```ts
import { createCliArgsParser, generateCliOptions } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const defs = generateCliOptions(schema, {
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    scope: 'cli',
    output: 'cli-options.json',
});
const parser = createCliArgsParser(defs);
parser.parse(['--base-url', 'http://localhost:8080']);
```

Options: `scope` (default `cli`), `output`, `shortFlags`, `envPathOf`.

## CLI program

The preferred entry point is `engine.cli.program.create()`. It derives options
from the engine schema, infers `run` values and accepts the full program options:

```ts
const program = engine.cli.program.create(
    cmd => [
        cmd('serve')
            .description('Run the server.')
            .option({ flags: '--json', description: 'Print JSON.' })
            .run(({ config, values, context }) => {
                // config: the validated `serve` section
                // values: the explicit CLI values
                // context: the host command context
            }),
    ],
    {
        name: 'myapp',
        globalOptions: [{ flags: '--json', description: 'Print JSON.' }],
        disableColors: ({ color }) => color === false,
    }
);
await program.invokeAsync();
```

`engine.cli.program.create()` accepts `argv`, `name`, `description`, `version`,
`globalOptions`, `context`, `disableColors`, `writeOut`, `writeErr` and
`format`. See the
[API reference](/guide/config-generator/api#program-members-and-options)
for `invoke`/`invokeAsync`, hooks, help/error formatting and `bin`.

Without an engine, `generateConfigProgram(schema, options)` returns the same
`CliCommand[]`; each command spec runs with the validated scope config. It
requires `envPrefix`; `envPathOf`, `commands`, `includePaths`, `excludePaths`,
`flags`, `descriptions` and `types` shape the generated commands. When `commands`
is omitted, one command is generated per command-eligible scope
(`cliCommand: false` opts a scope out).

```ts
import { generateConfigProgram } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const commands = generateConfigProgram(schema, {
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    includePaths: ['server', 'server.port'],
});
```

Use the lower-level `createConfigProgram(commands, options?)` only when you
already have a command list that is not tied to an engine; it accepts the same
program options.

## CLI docs

`generateCliDocs(commands, options?)` renders a markdown reference from
`CliCommand` descriptors. It is standalone because it does not read a
config schema:

```ts
import { builtinCommands } from '@deltabox/toolchain/cli';
import { generateCliDocs } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const markdown = generateCliDocs([...builtinCommands(), ...myCommands], {
    title: 'CLI reference',
    intro: 'Generated from the registered commands.',
    prefix: 'my-cli',
    outline: [2, 3],
});
```

Hidden commands are omitted, duplicate names keep the first descriptor, and
args/options/defaults are rendered like the `dbx` reference. Pass the result
through `formatGenerated(..., { fileName: 'cli.md' })` to format it.

## Formatting

```ts
import { formatGenerated } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const formatted = await formatGenerated(source, {
    fileName: 'config.ts', // infers the language
    options: { printWidth: 100 }, // merged over GENERATED_FORMAT_OPTIONS
});
```

`formatGenerated` is best-effort: it returns the input unchanged when no
formatter is available.

## Advanced

### Post-process generated output

Generators return strings or records, so you can transform them before writing:

```ts
import fs from 'node:fs';

import { formatGenerated, generateConfigTypes } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const files = generateConfigTypes(schema, { baseGroup: 'base' });
for (const [scope, source] of Object.entries(files)) {
    const withBanner = `// Generated from schemas/${scope}.ts — do not edit.\n${source}`;
    const formatted = await formatGenerated(withBanner, { fileName: `${scope}.ts` });
    fs.mkdirSync('types', { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(`types/${scope}.ts`, formatted);
}
```

### Custom headers, imports and overrides

```ts
generateConfigTypes(schema, {
    header: '/* eslint-disable */',
    imports: ["import type { AppEnv } from './env.js';"],
    overrides: {
        ServerConfig: 'export interface ServerConfig extends BaseServer {}',
    },
});
```

`overrides` is keyed by the generated type name and replaces the whole
declaration, so keep the `imports`/`header` options handy for types the schema
cannot express.

### Dry runs

Every generator accepts `outputDir: false` / `output: false`:

```ts
generateConfigTypes(schema, { outputDir: false });
await generateConfigJsonSchema(schema, { output: false });
```

The grouped `.write()` methods always write; use the `.generate()` methods when
you only need the content.

### Engine vs standalone

The engine form injects the bound options; the standalone form takes them
explicitly. They produce the same output:

```ts
const engine = createConfigEngine({
    schema,
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    baseGroup: 'base',
});

engine.markdown.generate(); // uses the bound options

generateConfigMarkdown(schema, {
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    baseGroup: 'base',
});
```

See [Generated outputs](/guide/config-generator/generated-outputs) for the shape
of each file, [CLI commands](/guide/config-generator/cli-commands) for the
`config:*` descriptors, and the [API reference](/guide/config-generator/api) for
the complete export list.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config-generator/cli-commands.md
---
# CLI commands docs

`configCommands({ engine, defaults })` returns typed `CliCommand[]`; register
them on the engine program with `engine.cli.program.create()` (preferred), or on
a program built with the lower-level `createConfigProgram()` if the command list
is not tied to an engine. They generate config artifacts:

| Command           | Writes                                       |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `config:env`      | `.env.example`                               |
| `config:types`    | config types (`--env` also writes env types) |
| `config:json`     | `config.json` (metadata)                     |
| `config:schema`   | `config.schema.json`                         |
| `config:markdown` | the markdown reference                       |
| `config:cli`      | `cli-options.json`                           |
| `config:all`      | everything, under one output directory       |

```ts
import { configCommands } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const commands = configCommands({
    engine,
    defaults: { typesDir: 'packages/shared/src/types', docsDir: 'docs/reference' },
});
const program = engine.cli.program.create(() => commands, { name: 'myapp' });
await program.invokeAsync();
```

> These commands are library-only: `dbx` itself does not register a `config:*`
> group, because each command needs a `ConfigEngine` bound to your schema. Add
> the returned commands to your own program.

The `config:*` commands generate config artifacts; they do not write the CLI
reference. For that, pass the command descriptors your CLI registers to
[`generateCliDocs()` or `engine.markdown.cli.write()`](/guide/config-generator/generate#cli-docs).

## Deriving flags from config fields

When a command flag maps to a config field, generate the option from the schema
instead of hand-writing its flag, description and default. The recommended
entry point is `engine.cli.program.create()`:

```ts
const { commands } = engine.cli.program.create(cmd => [
    cmd('tsconfig')
        .description('Generate workspace tsconfig files.')
        // Genuine runtime flags stay explicit (the escape hatch).
        .options([
            { flags: '--cwd <dir>', description: 'Repo root.' },
            { flags: '--json', description: 'Print the resolved config.' },
        ])
        .run(({ config }) => {
            // `config` is the validated `tsconfig` section.
        }),
]);
```

Config-backed flags are derived recursively: objects and union object branches
expand to dotted paths (`sync.format` → `--format-*`), scalar arrays become list
flags, and arrays of objects/records/maps are skipped unless the field defines
`cli` metadata. Use `engine.cli.program.createCommand(scope, spec)` when you want the
runtime `values` object inferred from the command's `options` list;
`createCommand('name', spec)` / `cmd('name', spec)` build a runtime-only command
with no config scope. Metadata lives in the schema:

```ts
port: z.number().default(3000).meta({ cli: { short: 'p' } }),
aliases: z.boolean().default(true).meta({
    cli: { flag: '--no-aliases', type: 'boolean', description: 'Skip path aliases.' },
}),
internal: z.string().meta({ cli: false }),
format: z.union([z.boolean(), z.object({ fix: z.boolean() })]).meta({
    cliCommand: { name: 'format', description: 'Format the managed files.' },
}),
```

`cli: false` removes a field (and its subtree) from generated flags without
hiding it from env/types/docs. `cliCommand: false` opts a scope out of automatic
command generation. Env exposure still comes from `envName`/`envPath`; set
`envExpose: false` for CLI-only values. Runtime-only flags (`--cwd`, `--json`,
`--force`, `--dry-run`, output selectors) always stay in the command spec; an
option with a `path` intentionally maps a runtime flag back to a config field.

The lower-level helpers remain available for existing descriptors:

```ts
import { configCliOptions } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const options = [
    { flags: '--json', description: 'Print the resolved config.' },
    ...configCliOptions(tsconfigConfigSchema),
];
```

Config defaults are applied by the command context, so only explicitly typed
flags are forwarded. `configCliCommand` wraps the same generation with parsing
and validation when the whole command is config-shaped. Use `includePaths` /
`excludePaths` only as a narrow escape hatch; a flag that is not a config field
(output mode, `--cwd`, `--restore`, provider options) stays hand-written and
documented as runtime-only.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config-generator/load-the-config.md
---
# Load the config at runtime

Generation is only half of it: the same schema loads the value back. The runtime
parsers read the `envName` / `cli` metadata, coerce env and CLI strings,
merge overrides and validate the result through the schema, so the returned
object matches the generated types.

```ts
import { parseCliConfig, parseConfig, parseEnvConfig } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

// MYAPP_HOST, MYAPP_PORT, ... -> { host: '0.0.0.0', port: 3000 }
const fromEnv = parseEnvConfig(serverConfig, process.env, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });

// env + CLI (argv defaults to `process.argv.slice(2)`), overrides merged on top
const config = parseConfig(serverConfig, { host: '127.0.0.1' }, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });

// CLI only: `--port 8080 --host localhost`
const fromCli = parseCliConfig(serverConfig, process.argv.slice(2), { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });
```

| Export                                                  | Sources                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `parseConfig(schema, overrides?, opts?)`                | env + CLI, with `overrides` merged last and validated    |
| `parseEnvConfig(schema, env?, opts?)`                   | env only                                                 |
| `parseCliConfig(schema, argv?, opts?)`                  | CLI only                                                 |
| `collect(schema, opts?)`                                | env + CLI, no overrides (pass `validate: true` to check) |
| `loadConfig(options)` / `loadConfigAsync(options)`      | file + env + CLI, then `overrides`, then validation      |
| `loadEnvConfig*` / `loadCliConfig*` / `loadFileConfig*` | file plus env, CLI or neither                            |
| `loadConfigSync(options)`                               | the sync subset (JSON/YAML/CJS and sync loaders)         |

`source` accepts one source or an ordered array (`['env', 'cli']`) on both the
parsers and the loaders. A loader always reads its file; the remaining sources
layer over it. The precedence is **file -> env -> CLI -> overrides ->
validation**. Parsers are the pure API: `parseConfig` starts from the value you
pass as `overrides`, not from a file.

Async variants (`parseConfigAsync`, `parseEnvConfigAsync`, `parseCliConfigAsync`)
accept a promise for the env source, argv or overrides; the `*Sync` aliases keep
the synchronous call shape.

## Scopes

Parsing the engine's `schema` returns the nested `{ server, frontend }` object;
parsing one scope's schema returns that scope's fields directly:

```ts
const scoped = parseEnvConfig(engine.schema, process.env, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });
// { server: { port: 8080, host: '0.0.0.0' } }

const server = parseEnvConfig(serverConfig, process.env, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });
// { port: 8080, host: '0.0.0.0' }
```

The same works for untyped and plain/primitive schemas:

```ts
const untyped = {
    type: 'object',
    properties: {
        port: { type: 'number', default: 3000, envName: 'MYAPP_PORT' },
        host: { type: 'string', default: 'localhost' },
    },
};

parseEnvConfig(untyped, { MYAPP_PORT: '4000' }); // { port: 4000, host: 'localhost' }

const plain = { server: { port: 3000, host: 'localhost' } };
parseEnvConfig(plain, { APP_SERVER_PORT: '4000' });
// { server: { port: 4000, host: 'localhost' } }
```

## Common options

Every parser shares the collect options:

* `envPrefix` — the prefix stripped from env names (default `APP_`, `null` disables it).
* `envSource` / `argv` — the env record and argument list to read (defaults to
  `process.env` and `process.argv.slice(2)`).
* `include` / `exclude` — path globs (`server.*`, `**.port`) or presence kinds
  (`required`, `defined`, `undefined`, `null`).
* `validate` — parse the resolved value through the schema (the `parse*` family
  defaults to `true`).
* `errorOptions` — `errorLevel` (`throw`/`warn`/`silent`), `logger`,
  `rewriteMessage`, `defaultMessage` and `trigger` for validation problems.
  A thrown problem is a `ConfigParseError`.
* `envPathOf` — override env-name -> dotted-path derivation (eg. dual prefixes).

Env names come from `.meta({ envName })`; without it, the prefix plus the field
path is used (`MYAPP_SERVER_PORT`). CLI flags come from `.meta({ cli: { flag } })`
(or the legacy `cliFlag`), falling back to `--server-port`.

## Load from a file

`loadConfig` / `loadConfigAsync` discover a config file (plus JSON/YAML/custom
loaders), import it, layer env vars and CLI args over the file value, merge
`overrides`, and validate through the passed `parser` (or `schema`). The
loaders are the preferred loading API; you do **not** need to call `parseConfig`,
`parseEnvConfig` or `parseCliConfig` afterwards.

```ts
import { loadConfigAsync } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const loaded = await loadConfigAsync({
    parser: serverConfig,
    cwd: process.cwd(),
    // Discovery (flat fields; `configFileOptions` also works)
    locations: ['.', '.myapp'],
    names: ['dbx.config.ts', 'dbx.config.js'],
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    // Sources: file -> env -> CLI -> overrides -> validation
    source: ['file', 'env', 'cli'],
    overrides: { host: '127.0.0.1' },
    validate: true,
});

if (loaded) {
    console.log(loaded.path, loaded.config); // the file and the parsed value
}
```

The source-specific loaders make the intent explicit:

```ts
import { loadCliConfig, loadEnvConfig, loadFileConfig } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

await loadFileConfig({ parser: serverConfig }); // file only
await loadEnvConfig({ parser: serverConfig }); // file + env
await loadCliConfig({ parser: serverConfig }); // file + CLI
```

Each loader also has `*Sync` and `*Async` variants. Pass `source: 'env'` (or
`['env', 'cli']`) to `loadConfig*` when you want a custom combination. Unknown
sources are ignored by the collector, so the loaders remain safe when an
application only enables one.

Without a `parser`/`schema` the raw file value is returned unchanged (there is
no schema to map env or CLI names onto):

```ts
const raw = await loadConfig({ cwd: process.cwd() });
```

### Default file names

The generic config package looks for neutral names: `config.ts`, `config.mts`,
`config.cts`, `config.js`, `config.mjs`, `config.cjs` and `config.json` in
`.`, `config` and `configs`. It never defaults to `dbx.config.*`. An
application that owns a filename passes `names` or
`configFileOptions: { filename: 'myapp.config' }` explicitly.

Options include `configFileOptions` (filename, extensions, locations,
`packageJson`, ancestor search), `required`, `overrides`, `source`, `fresh`
(re-import in watch mode), `tsconfig` (path-alias resolution for TS configs) and
`loader`. `loadConfigSync` supports JSON/YAML/CJS and synchronous loaders;
`loadConfigAsync` also supports ESM and TypeScript.

> The dotted path is the env name with the prefix removed and `_` folded to `.`,
> so `MYAPP_AUTH_TOKEN_TTL` reads as `auth.token.ttl`. Env names live on the
> schema as `.meta({ envName })`, so the generated `.env` file and the runtime
> parser stay in step.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config-generator/generated-outputs.md
---
# Generated outputs

Every generator reads from the same Zod, untyped or plain-value schema. The
engine's own config model is the living example: its types are committed at
[packages/shared/src/config-types.ts](https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/blob/main/packages/shared/src/config-types.ts).

For the engine/standalone call forms and the full option list per generator, see
[Generate](/guide/config-generator/generate). For every export and option, see
the [API reference](/guide/config-generator/api).

## Config types — `engine.types` / `generateConfigTypes()`

Named `interface`s (and `type` aliases for enums/unions) with jsdoc taken from
`.describe()`. Unions and refs stay named, so nested objects are referenced
rather than inlined:

```ts
// engine.types.generate() -> { server: "...", cli: "..." }
engine.types.write({ outputDir: 'types' }); // types/server.ts, types/cli.ts
```

```ts
// types/server.ts
export interface ServerConfig {
    /** Bind host. */
    host?: string;
    port?: number;
    auth?: { password?: string; enabled?: boolean };
}
```

An object schema that also accepts arbitrary keys (Zod `.catchall(...)`,
`.loose()` or `z.looseObject(...)`, ie. `additionalProperties` in the JSON
Schema) generates an open interface with an index signature, so the extra keys
stay typed as `unknown` instead of being rejected:

```ts
export interface ServerConfig {
    /** Bind host. */
    host?: string;
    [key: string]: unknown;
}
```

## Markdown — `engine.markdown` / `generateConfigMarkdown()`

One reference page per scope plus an index listing the required/core env vars:

```ts
engine.markdown.write({ outputDir: 'docs/reference/configuration' });
// docs/reference/configuration/server.md, .../index.md
```

See a real full example at [config/reference.md](../../config/reference.md).

Markdown frontmatter is enabled by default. Set `frontmatter: false` to omit it,
pass a raw string to replace the body, or pass a callback to build it from the
generator options. The returned string is wrapped in `---` automatically.

```ts
generateConfigMarkdown(schema, {
    frontmatter: ctx => `title: ${ctx.options.title ?? 'Configuration'}`,
});
```

Use `combined: true` to render every scope into one file instead of one file per
scope. `generateConfigTypes`, `generateConfigMarkdown` and `generateConfigEnv`
return file contents and only write when `outputDir`/`output` is a string;
`false` explicitly disables writing.

## Env — `engine.env` / `generateEnvFile()`

A `.env.example`; secrets are emitted commented out so operators fill them in:

```ts
engine.env.write({ output: '.env.example' });
```

```sh
# ---- SERVER ----
MYAPP_HOST=localhost
# MYAPP_AUTH_PASSWORD=
```

## JSON Schema — `engine.jsonSchema` / `generateConfigJsonSchema()`

The resolved untyped JSON Schema for every scope, for editor autocomplete:

```ts
await engine.jsonSchema.write({ output: 'config.schema.json' });
```

## CLI docs - `engine.markdown.cli` / `generateCliDocs()`

`generateCliDocs` reads `CliCommand` descriptors rather than the config
schema: it renders a markdown reference from the commands your CLI actually
registers. The engine exposes the same generator as
`engine.markdown.cli.generate()` (and `.write()`):

```ts
import { builtinCommands } from '@deltabox/toolchain/cli';

const markdown = engine.markdown.cli.generate([...builtinCommands(), ...myCommands], {
    prefix: 'my-cli',
    title: 'CLI reference',
    intro: 'Generated from the registered commands.',
});

engine.markdown.cli.write(builtinCommands(), { output: 'docs/cli.md' });
```

The standalone `generateCliDocs(commands, options)` export is equivalent when you
do not already have an engine. Hidden commands are omitted and duplicate names
keep the first descriptor. The `dbx` reference itself is generated this way, so a
custom command no longer has to be added to `builtinCommands()` to be documented.

## Env docs - `engine.markdown.env` / `generateEnvMarkdown()`

`engine.markdown.env.generate()` renders the environment-variable table from
`engine.collect()`, using the engine's `envPrefix`. `write({ output })` writes the
page:

```ts
engine.markdown.env.write({ output: 'docs/env.md' });
```

## Single pages - `engine.markdown.file` / `generateMarkdownFile()`

`engine.markdown.file` renders one page with frontmatter and a `#` title. The
body is supplied by the caller, so it is useful for overview/index pages:

```ts
engine.markdown.file.write({
    output: 'docs/index.md',
    title: 'Config types',
    body: 'The toolchain has three configuration surfaces...',
});
```

## Post-processing

The `generate*` functions return their content, so you can transform it before
writing (the grouped `.write()` methods write immediately):

```ts
const files = generateConfigTypes(schema);
for (const [scope, source] of Object.entries(files)) {
    const sourceWithBanner = `// Generated — do not edit.\n${source}`;
    await fs.promises.writeFile(`types/${scope}.ts`, sourceWithBanner);
}
```

If the transform changes the formatting, run the result through
[`formatGenerated()`](#formatting--formatgenerated) before writing.

## Formatting — `formatGenerated()`

Generated text is formatted **at generation time**, so a written file is already
formatted instead of relying on a separate `yarn fmt` pass. `formatGenerated`
runs source through Oxfmt, preferring the project-local `vite-plus/fmt` (Oxfmt
ships with Vite+), then `oxfmt`, and returns the input untouched when no formatter
is resolvable, so generation never fails on a missing formatter.

```ts
import { formatGenerated, GENERATED_FORMAT_OPTIONS } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const source = 'export const config={a:1}';
const formatted = await formatGenerated(source, {
    fileName: 'config.ts', // infers the language (default `generated.ts`)
    options: { printWidth: 100 }, // merged over GENERATED_FORMAT_OPTIONS
});
```

`GENERATED_FORMAT_OPTIONS` is the baseline Oxfmt config matching the toolchain's
own `vite.config.ts` (4-space indent, single quotes, `trailingComma: 'es5'`,
`jsdoc: true`, ...). Pass `options.fileName` to format JSON, markdown or another
language, and `options.options` to override any single option.

For a full, real example of the generated config types, see
`packages/shared/src/config-types.ts`.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config-generator/client-and-server.md
---
# Client and server configs

Config code is often shared between an API and a browser app. The schemas can
share primitives, but for best-practice the **engines**, loaders and runtime imports must stay in
their own context.

A client bundle should never pull in `node:*` (unless your bundler handles them), a server
secret, or the server config engine; a server process should not depend on
browser-only globals.

The safest structure is one folder per context, each with its own schema entry,
engine and public import path. Do not put a single barrel `index.ts` above both
contexts that re-exports their engines or schemas.

## Project layout

```tree
- name: packages/shared/src/config
  children:
    - name: common
      description: Context-free primitives only
      children:
        - name: primitives.ts
        - name: meta.ts
    - name: client
      description: Browser-safe config
      children:
        - name: schema
          children:
            - name: index.ts
              description: Client schemas only
            - name: api.ts
            - name: telemetry.ts
        - name: engine.ts
          description: createConfigEngine(client schemas)
        - name: index.ts
          description: Public client entry
    - name: server
      description: Server-only config
      children:
        - name: schema
          children:
            - name: index.ts
              description: Server schemas only
            - name: database.ts
            - name: http.ts
        - name: engine.ts
          description: createConfigEngine(server schemas)
        - name: index.ts
          description: Public server entry
    - name: index.ts
      status: deleted
      description: Never re-export both contexts
```

`common/` may be imported by either side, but it must stay free of runtime
dependencies such as `node:fs`, database clients or browser APIs. Everything
else is context-specific.

## Server context

### Server schemas

Keep each server schema module focused, and export only server schemas from the
server schema entry:

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/server/schema/database.ts
import { z } from 'zod';

export const databaseConfig = z.object({
    url: z.string().meta({
        envName: 'APP_DATABASE_URL',
        required: true,
        secret: true,
    }),
    poolSize: z.number().default(10).meta({ envName: 'APP_DATABASE_POOL_SIZE' }),
});
```

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/server/schema/http.ts
import { z } from 'zod';

export const httpConfig = z.object({
    port: z.number().default(3000).meta({ envName: 'APP_HTTP_PORT' }),
    trustProxy: z.boolean().default(false).meta({ envName: 'APP_HTTP_TRUST_PROXY' }),
});
```

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/server/schema/index.ts
export { databaseConfig } from './database.js';
export { httpConfig } from './http.js';
```

### Server engine

The server engine imports the server schema entry only:

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/server/engine.ts
import { createConfigEngine } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

import * as serverSchema from './schema/index.js';

export const serverConfig = createConfigEngine({
    schema: {
        database: serverSchema.databaseConfig,
        http: serverSchema.httpConfig,
    },
    envPrefix: 'APP_',
});
```

The public server entry is the only module the server application imports:

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/server/index.ts
export { serverConfig } from './engine.js';
export * from './schema/index.js';
```

### Loading server config

Read files and `process.env` in the server process:

```ts
import { serverConfig } from '@org/shared/config/server';

// apps/api/src/config.ts
import { loadConfigAsync, parseEnvConfig } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

export async function loadServerConfig() {
    // load config from file, cli and env
    const loaded = await loadConfigAsync({
        parser: serverConfig.schema,
        cwd: process.cwd(),
        names: ['dbx.config.ts', 'dbx.config.js'],
    });

    if (loaded) return loaded.config;

    // fallback to env config
    return parseEnvConfig(serverConfig.schema, process.env, {
        envPrefix: 'APP_',
    });
}
```

`loadConfigAsync` can import TypeScript and read the filesystem, so it must not
appear in a client module graph.

## Client context

### Client schema

Client schemas may only describe browser-visible values. Prefix public values
with the client-visible prefix (`PUBLIC_`), and keep secrets out entirely:

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/client/schema/api.ts
import { z } from 'zod';

export const apiConfig = z.object({
    baseUrl: z.string().default('/api').meta({ envName: 'PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL' }),
    timeout: z.number().default(10_000).meta({ envName: 'PUBLIC_API_TIMEOUT' }),
});
```

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/client/schema/telemetry.ts
import { z } from 'zod';

export const telemetryConfig = z.object({
    enabled: z.boolean().default(false).meta({ envName: 'PUBLIC_TELEMETRY_ENABLED' }),
});
```

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/client/schema/index.ts
export { apiConfig } from './api.js';
export { telemetryConfig } from './telemetry.js';
```

### Client engine

The client engine imports only the client schema entry:

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/client/engine.ts
import { createConfigEngine } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

import * as clientSchema from './schema/index.js';

export const clientConfig = createConfigEngine({
    schema: {
        api: clientSchema.apiConfig,
        telemetry: clientSchema.telemetryConfig,
    },
    envPrefix: 'PUBLIC_', // or VITE_, NEXT_
});
```

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/client/index.ts
export { clientConfig } from './engine.js';
export * from './schema/index.js';
```

### Loading client config

The browser has `import.meta.env`, not `process.env`, and it must not import
the server engine or `node:fs`:

```ts
import { clientConfig } from '@org/shared/config/client';

// apps/web/src/config.ts
import { parseEnvConfig } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

export const webConfig = parseEnvConfig(
    clientConfig.schema,
    import.meta.env as Record<string, string | undefined>,
    { envPrefix: 'PUBLIC_' }
);
```

Vite/Vite+ only exposes env vars with the configured public prefix; the schema
above uses `PUBLIC_` consistently. Never put a server secret in a client schema.

## Bundlers

Treeshaking depends on what a module **imports**, not on which exports you
happen to use. A top-level barrel defeats the split:

```tree
- name: packages/shared/src/config
  children:
    - name: index.ts
      status: deleted
      description: Re-exports client + server; every importer pulls both
    - name: client/index.ts
      description: Client-only entry
    - name: server/index.ts
      description: Server-only entry
```

Import the context entry explicitly:

```ts
// Bad:
// the barrel can load both engines into the same module graph
import { clientConfig } from '@org/shared/config';
// Good:
// the client graph only sees the client engine
import { clientConfig } from '@org/shared/config/client';
```

Expose separate package subpaths instead of one mixed entry:

```json [package.json]
{
    "exports": {
        "./config/client": "./dist/config/client/index.js",
        "./config/server": "./dist/config/server/index.js"
    },
    "sideEffects": false
}
```

### Side effects and boundaries

Treeshaking cannot remove a module with import-time side effects. Keep the config
modules declarative:

* Do not open database connections, read files or start servers at module load.
* Do not import `node:*` from the client schema or client engine (unless your bundler handles them).
* Do not import the client engine from the server engine, or vice versa.
* Keep `createConfigEngine` calls in the context's `engine.ts`; import that file
  only from the matching side.
* If a package needs a server-only guard, make the server entry the only one
  that imports the server dependencies. A client import of the server entry
  should fail at build time, not silently bundle it.

### A correct import graph

```tree
- name: apps/web/src/config.ts
  description: imports @org/shared/config/client only
  status: added
- name: apps/api/src/config.ts
  description: imports @org/shared/config/server only
  status: added
```

The client bundle never reaches `server/engine.ts`, `server/schema/*` or
`node:*` (unless your bundler handles them); the server process never reaches `client/schema/*` or
`import.meta.env` parsing.

## Checklist

* One schema folder and one engine per context.
* No `config/index.ts` that re-exports both context engines.
* Client code imports only `config/client`; server code imports only
  `config/server`.
* Shared `common` modules are context-free.
* Client schemas use only public config options and no secrets.
* Server-only modules are never imported from client code.
* `sideEffects: false` plus no import-time side effects, so unused context
  modules are actually removed.

See [Load the config](/guide/config-generator/load-the-config) for the parser
and loader options, and the [API reference](/guide/config-generator/api) for the full API.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config-generator/real-world-shape.md
---
# Real-world shape

A real project usually has **two engines**, one per runtime context, rather than
one engine that mixes server and browser settings:

* a server engine with database, HTTP and secret-bearing schemas;
* a client engine with public API URLs, feature flags and other browser-safe
  values.

Keeping them in separate folders and entry points is what lets bundlers drop the
server engine from the browser bundle (and vice versa). See
[Client and server](/guide/config-generator/client-and-server) for the full
layout and bundler guidance.

## Server engine

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/server/engine.ts
import { createConfigEngine } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

import * as serverSchema from './schema/index.js';

export const serverConfig = createConfigEngine({
    schema: {
        database: serverSchema.databaseConfig,
        http: serverSchema.httpConfig,
    },
    envPrefix: 'APP_',
    baseGroup: ['base', 'http'],
    root: monorepoRoot(),
});
```

## Client engine

```ts
// packages/shared/src/config/client/engine.ts
import { createConfigEngine } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

import * as clientSchema from './schema/index.js';

export const clientConfig = createConfigEngine({
    schema: {
        api: clientSchema.apiConfig,
        telemetry: clientSchema.telemetryConfig,
    },
    envPrefix: 'PUBLIC_',
});
```

## Generation

Run the generators against each engine so each context's `.env.example`, types,
JSON Schema and markdown reference stay scoped to its own schema:

```ts
import { configCommands } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

import { clientConfig } from './client/engine.js';
import { serverConfig } from './server/engine.js';

export const commands = [
    ...configCommands({
        engine: serverConfig,
        defaults: { envDir: 'config/server' },
    }),
    ...configCommands({
        engine: clientConfig,
        defaults: { envDir: 'config/client' },
    }),
];
```

If the project exposes one `config:all` command, call the generators for both
engines explicitly. Do not build a single engine whose schema imports both
`server/` and `client/` modules.

## Loading

At runtime, each context loads its own engine:

```ts
import { serverConfig } from '@org/shared/config/server';

// apps/api/src/config.ts (server)
import { loadConfigAsync } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const loaded = await loadConfigAsync({ parser: serverConfig.schema });
```

```ts
import { clientConfig } from '@org/shared/config/client';

// apps/web/src/config.ts (client)
import { parseEnvConfig } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

export const webConfig = parseEnvConfig(
    clientConfig.schema,
    import.meta.env as Record<string, string | undefined>,
    { envPrefix: 'PUBLIC_' }
);
```

`loadConfig*` loads a file and layers env/CLI over it (`loadEnvConfig*` and
`loadCliConfig*` select one explicitly). Use `parseEnvConfig`/`parseCliConfig`/
`parseConfig` when there is no file and you are parsing a pure source.

## Keep the boundaries clean

* Import `@org/shared/config/client` from browser code and
  `@org/shared/config/server` from server code.
* Never create a `packages/shared/src/config/index.ts` that re-exports both
  engines.
* Keep shared `common` modules context-free (no `node:*` unless your bundler handles them, no secrets, no
  browser-only globals).
* Mark config packages as side-effect free and avoid import-time connections or
  file reads.
* Client schemas use public config options only; server secrets never enter the
  client schema.

These `config:*` commands belong to the consumer's own CLI; `dbx` itself does
not expose them.

See [Client and server](/guide/config-generator/client-and-server) for the
complete folder layout, import graph and bundler checklist, and the
[API reference](/guide/config-generator/api) for every generator and runtime
export.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config-generator/api.md
---
# API reference

Everything is exported from the `@deltabox/toolchain/config` subpath. The engine
and the standalone functions share the same schemas and options, so you can start
with the engine and drop to a single generator when you only need one artifact.

```ts
import {
    ConfigProgramError,
    createConfigEngine,
    createConfigProgram,
    generateConfigProgram,
    generateConfigTypes,
    parseConfig,
    parseEnvConfig,
    loadConfigAsync,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';
```

## Schemas

A schema is a Zod schema, a resolved untyped schema, or a plain value. Plain
objects and primitives are supported through their defaults.

```ts
import { z } from 'zod';

// Zod (the richest form: validation + defaults + metadata)
const zodSchema = z.object({
    port: z.number().default(3000).meta({ envName: 'MYAPP_PORT' }),
});

// Untyped/JSON-Schema shape
const untypedSchema = {
    type: 'object',
    properties: {
        port: { type: 'number', default: 3000, envName: 'MYAPP_PORT' },
        host: { type: 'string', default: 'localhost' },
    },
};

// Plain object (values become defaults)
const plainObject = {
    port: 3000,
    host: 'localhost',
};

// A primitive scope (the value becomes the default)
const plainPrimitive = 3000;
```

A **scope map** keys each top-level entry by scope name:

```ts
const scopes = {
    server: zodSchema,
    frontend: { apiUrl: 'http://localhost:8080' },
    cli: 3000,
};
```

A single schema (Zod or untyped) is treated as one runtime scope named `config`.
Arrays of schemas are merged into one scope.

```ts
const engine = createConfigEngine({ schema: scopes, baseGroup: ['base', 'server'] });
```

The `baseGroup` option accepts a string or an array of strings. Each named group
is hoisted into the generated `...Base` interface (types) and the flattened
markdown/JSON Schema shape. Multiple groups are merged in declaration order.

## Engine

`createConfigEngine(options)` binds the schema once and exposes the generators.

```ts
const engine = createConfigEngine({
    schema: scopes,
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    baseGroup: ['base', 'server'],
    root: process.cwd(),
    envPathOf: env =>
        env
            .replace(/^MYAPP_/, '')
            .toLowerCase()
            .replace(/_/g, '.'),
});

engine.schema; // the exact schema passed in
engine.envPrefix; // 'MYAPP_'
engine.baseGroup; // ['base', 'server']
engine.root; // process.cwd()
```

| Member                  | Returns                                        |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `engine.collect()`      | every collected `ConfigDef`                    |
| `engine.requiredVars()` | the `required` definitions (optionally scoped) |

### `engine.env`

```ts
const envFile = engine.env.generate({ envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });
// MYAPP_PORT=3000

const envTypes = engine.env.types.generate({ outputDir: 'types' });
// { 'env.ts': '...', 'dbx-env.d.ts': '...' }

engine.env.write({ output: '.env.example' });
engine.env.types.write({ outputDir: 'types' }); // returns the written paths
```

### `engine.types`

```ts
const files = engine.types.generate({ outputDir: 'types' });
// { server: 'export interface ServerConfig...', cli: '...' }

engine.types.write({ outputDir: 'types', extension: 'mts' });
```

### `engine.markdown`

```ts
const commands = [/* your CliCommand descriptors */];

const pages = engine.markdown.generate({ outputDir: 'docs/reference' });
// { 'server.md': '...', 'cli.md': '...', 'index.md': '...' }

// One combined page instead of one per scope
engine.markdown.generate({ combined: true }); // { 'index.md': '...' }

// A CLI command reference
engine.markdown.cli.generate(commands);
engine.markdown.cli.write(commands, { output: 'docs/cli.md' });

// The environment-variable reference
engine.markdown.env.generate();
engine.markdown.env.write({ output: 'docs/env.md' });

// One generic page
engine.markdown.file.generate({ title: 'Docs', body: 'Hello.' });
```

### `engine.cli`

```ts
// Env-backed `cli` scope options
const options = engine.cli.generate({ scope: 'cli' });
// [{ flag: '--port', env: 'MYAPP_PORT', type: 'number', ... }]

engine.cli.write({ output: 'cli-options.json' });

// Scoped config commands + options from every config field
const scoped = engine.cli.options();
// {
//   command: { server: { name: 'server', type: 'object', options: [...] }, ... },
//   commandEntries: [['server', {...}], ...],
//   options: [...],
//   optionsEntries: [['--port', {...}], ...],
//   diagnostics: [...],
// }

// The high-level program: chained commands with schema-derived flags + typed config
const { commands } = engine.cli.program.create(cmd => [
    cmd('server')
        .option({ flags: '--json', description: 'Print JSON.' })
        .run(({ config, values, context }) => {
            // `config` is the resolved `server` section.
        }),
]);
```

### `engine.jsonSchema`

`jsonSchema` is async because Zod's JSON Schema lowering is async.

```ts
const doc = await engine.jsonSchema.generate({ preserveDefs: true });
await engine.jsonSchema.write({ output: 'config.schema.json' });
```

### `engine.configJson`

```ts
const metadata = engine.configJson.build();
// { env: [...], cli: [...], config: [...] }
```

## Standalone generators

Every engine method has a standalone equivalent. They return content unless you
pass an output path/directory.

```ts
import {
    collectDefinitions,
    formatGenerated,
    generateCliDocs,
    generateCliOptions,
    generateConfigEnv,
    generateConfigJsonSchema,
    generateConfigMarkdown,
    generateConfigProgram,
    generateConfigTypes,
    generateEnvFile,
    generateEnvMarkdown,
    generateJsonSchemaFile,
    generateMarkdownFile,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

generateEnvFile(schema, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });
generateConfigEnv(schema, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_', outputDir: 'types' });
generateConfigTypes(schema, { outputDir: 'types' });
generateConfigMarkdown(schema, { outputDir: 'docs/reference' });
generateEnvMarkdown(collectDefinitions(schema, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' }));
generateMarkdownFile({ title: 'Docs', body: 'Hello.' });
generateCliOptions(schema, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_', scope: 'cli' });
generateCliDocs(commands, { output: 'docs/cli.md' });
const generated = generateConfigProgram(schema, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });

await generateConfigJsonSchema(schema, { baseGroup: ['base', 'server'] });
await generateJsonSchemaFile(schema, { output: 'config.schema.json' });

const formatted = await formatGenerated(source, { fileName: 'config.ts' });
```

## Runtime collection

`collect` resolves env vars and CLI args into a config object. It does not
validate unless `validate: true`.

```ts
import { collect, collectDefinitions, collectRequired } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const config = collect(schema, {
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    envSource: process.env,
    argv: process.argv.slice(2),
    validate: true,
});

const definitions = collectDefinitions(schema, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });
const required = collectRequired(schema, 'server');
```

## Runtime parsers

The parsers merge the enabled sources, apply overrides and validate by default.
`source` accepts `'file' | 'env' | 'cli'` or an ordered array such as
`['env', 'cli']`. All of them accept Zod, untyped and plain/primitive schemas.

```ts
import {
    parseCliConfig,
    parseConfig,
    parseEnvConfig,
    parseConfigAsync,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

// env + CLI + overrides
const config = parseConfig(schema, { port: 4000 }, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });

// env only
parseEnvConfig(schema, process.env, { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });

// CLI only: --port 4000 --host localhost
parseCliConfig(schema, process.argv.slice(2), { envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });

// An explicit source set
parseConfig(schema, {}, { source: ['env', 'cli'], envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });

// Async variants accept promise inputs
await parseConfigAsync(schema, Promise.resolve({ port: 4000 }));
```

`ConfigParseError` is thrown when validation fails and
`errorOptions.errorLevel` is `throw` (the default). Its `issues` array contains
the validated paths and messages.

## Loaders

`loadConfig*` discover a config file, import it, layer env vars and CLI args over
the file value, merge `overrides` and validate through the passed `parser` (or
`schema`). The precedence is **file -> env -> CLI -> overrides -> validation**.
You do **not** need to call `parseConfig`/`parseEnvConfig`/`parseCliConfig` after
`loadConfig*`: it already did that for you. Use the parsers when you have no file
to load.

```ts
import { loadConfig, loadConfigAsync, loadConfigSync } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const loaded = await loadConfigAsync({
    parser: z.object({
        port: z.number().default(3000),
        host: z.string().default('localhost'),
    }),
    cwd: process.cwd(),
    names: ['dbx.config.ts', 'dbx.config.js'],
    locations: ['.', 'config'],
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    source: ['file', 'env', 'cli'], // the default
    validate: true, // default when a parser is provided
});

loaded?.config; // the parsed + validated value
loaded?.path; // the file that was loaded
```

The source-specific family makes the selection explicit:

| Loader            | Sources                    |
| ----------------- | -------------------------- |
| `loadConfig*`     | file + env + CLI (default) |
| `loadEnvConfig*`  | file + env                 |
| `loadCliConfig*`  | file + CLI                 |
| `loadFileConfig*` | file only                  |

Each has `Sync` and `Async` variants. `source` also accepts a union on the
loaders, so `source: ['env', 'cli']` is equivalent to the default.

Without a `parser`/`schema`, the raw loaded value is returned:

```ts
const raw = await loadConfig({ cwd: process.cwd() });
```

The parser-based loader also accepts the flat discovery fields (`cwd`, `names`,
`locations`, `packageJsonKeys`, `parent`, `accept`, `tsconfig`, `fresh`) as well
as `configFileOptions` when you need the full discovery shape.

The default discovery names are neutral (`config.ts`, `config.js`,
`config.json`, ...), never `dbx.config.*`. Pass `names` or
`configFileOptions.filename` for an application-specific name.

`loadConfigSync` supports JSON/YAML/CJS and custom synchronous loaders;
`loadConfigAsync` also supports ESM and TypeScript.

`createConfigFile({ cwd, name?, content?, imports?, overwrite? })` writes a
starter `dbx.config.ts`.

## Schema utilities

```ts
import {
    compileZodSchema,
    flattenBaseSchema,
    isSchemaType,
    isZodSchema,
    metaOf,
    normalizeBaseGroups,
    normalizeConfigSchema,
    resolveUntypedSchema,
    splitBaseSchema,
    toSchemaType,
    zodToJsonSchema,
    zodToSchemaMap,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

isZodSchema(value); // Zod schema?
isSchemaType(value); // resolved untyped schema?

toSchemaType(schema); // Zod/plain value -> resolved untyped schema
resolveUntypedSchema({ port: 3000 }); // -> { properties: { port: { type: 'number', default: 3000 } } }
normalizeConfigSchema(schema); // -> { [scope]: resolvedSchema }
zodToJsonSchema(zodSchema); // -> untyped JSON Schema
zodToSchemaMap(zodSchema); // -> { [typeName]: resolvedSchema }
compileZodSchema(zodSchema); // best-effort Zod compile

normalizeBaseGroups(['base', 'server']); // ['base', 'server']
splitBaseSchema(schema, ['base', 'server']); // { base, groups, hasBase }
flattenBaseSchema(schema, ['base', 'server']); // base fields hoisted
metaOf(schema); // ConfigMeta | undefined
```

`renderTsType(node)` and `normalizeJsonSchemaMetadata(node)` are lower-level
helpers for custom JSON Schema pipelines.

## Environment helpers

```ts
import {
    envBool,
    envInt,
    envList,
    envMap,
    envPathOf,
    envString,
    envVarNameOf,
    parseEnvTree,
    readEnvPath,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const tree = parseEnvTree(process.env, 'MYAPP_');
envString(tree, 'host', 'localhost');
envInt(tree, 'port', 3000);
envBool(tree, 'debug', false);
envList(tree, 'tags', []);
envMap(tree, 'headers.map');
readEnvPath(tree, 'auth.token');

envPathOf('MYAPP_AUTH_TOKEN', 'MYAPP_'); // auth.token
envVarNameOf('auth.token', 'MYAPP_'); // MYAPP_AUTH_TOKEN
```

## CLI generation

`generateConfigCliOptions(schema)` walks the config fields (not just env-backed
values) and treats each **schema scope as a CLI command**, with its fields as
options. It returns scoped and flat views:

```ts
import {
    configCliCommand,
    generateConfigCliOptions,
    toToolchainOptions,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const result = generateConfigCliOptions(scopes, {
    includePaths: ['server', 'frontend.origin'], // optional path filter
    excludePaths: ['frontend.secrets'],
    flags: { 'auto.aliases': '--aliases' }, // optional custom mapping
    types: { auto: 'boolean' }, // override an ambiguous schema type
});

result.command.server; // { name: 'server', type: 'object', options: [...] }
result.commandEntries; // [['server', {...}], ['frontend', {...}]]
result.options; // every option across every command
result.optionsEntries; // [['--port', {...}], ...]

const options = toToolchainOptions(result.options);
// [{ flags: '--port <value>', description: 'HTTP port', default: '3000' }, ...]
```

`configCliCommand` builds a complete `CliCommand` from the schema, parses
the provided flags into a validated config and passes it to `run`:

```ts
import { configCliCommand } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

export const serveCommand = configCliCommand({
    name: 'serve',
    description: 'Run the API server.',
    schema: serverConfig,
    // Extra command-specific options that are not config fields.
    options: [{ flags: '--json', description: 'Print JSON.' }],
    run: (values, config, context) => {
        // `config` is already parsed/validated from `values`.
        console.log(config, context.config);
    },
});

// Build it into the engine program like any other CliCommand:
const program = engine.cli.program.create(() => [serveCommand]);
await program.invokeAsync();
```

For an existing command, prefer `engine.cli.program.create()` and keep only
genuinely non-config flags (output modes, `--cwd`, `--json`, `--restore`)
hand-written. The low-level `configCliOptions` one-liner remains available when
you already have a command descriptor:

```ts
import { configCliOptions } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const command = {
    name: 'tsconfig',
    description: 'Generate workspace tsconfig files.',
    options: [
        // The escape hatch: runtime selectors that are not config fields.
        { flags: '--cwd <dir>', description: 'Project root.' },
        { flags: '--json', description: 'Print the resolved config.' },
        // Config-backed options, generated recursively from the schema.
        ...configCliOptions(tsconfigConfigSchema),
    ],
    run: (values, context) => {
        // values from generated flags are available alongside custom flags
    },
};
```

### `engine.cli.program`

`engine.cli.generate()` and `engine.cli.options()` keep their low-level
behavior; `engine.cli.program.create()` is the command-level entry point:

```ts
const program = engine.cli.program.create(cmd => [
    cmd('serve')
        .description('Run the server.')
        .option({ flags: '--json', description: 'Print JSON.' })
        .option({ flags: '--listen <port>', path: 'port', type: 'number' })
        .command('serve', status =>
            status
                .name('status')
                .description('Print the resolved status.')
                .option({ flags: '--short', description: 'Short output.' })
                .run(({ config, values }) => {
                    // typed `serve` config + `short` value
                })
        )
        .run(({ config, values, context }) => {
            // config: the validated `serve` section
            // values: the explicit CLI values
            // context: the host CliCommandContext (dbx widens it to ToolchainCommandContext)
        }),
]);

await program.invokeAsync();
```

`create()` returns a built program: `program.commands` is the normalized command
list (a single command stays a single command; an empty list generates one
command per eligible scope). `createCommand(scope, spec)` builds one config-backed
command without a program; `cmd('name', spec)` / `createCommand('name', spec)`
build a runtime-only command without a config scope. The callback may be async;
`create()` then returns a promise.

`ConfigScopeCommand` chains support `name`, `description`, `version`, `argv`,
`bin`, `option`/`options`, `globalOption`/`globalOptions`, `inherit`,
`command`/`commands`, `subcommand`/`subcommands`, `onError` and terminal `run`.
`onError(error, context)` receives the loaded host context. Omit `run` for a
grouping command; it registers with its subcommands.

#### Program members and options

A `ConfigProgram` exposes the runtime surface:

| Member                                   | Description                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `commands`                               | The normalized commands (single command stays single).                 |
| `globals`                                | The program-level global options.                                      |
| `name()` / `description()` / `version()` | Set the metadata shown in help/version output.                         |
| `output(writeOut, writeErr?)`            | Route help/version output; `writeErr` is reserved for error rendering. |
| `globalOption()` / `globalOptions()`     | Append program-level globals.                                          |
| `argv(values)`                           | Set the explicit argv used by `invoke()`.                              |
| `withContext(context)`                   | Set the default host context.                                          |
| `configure(format)`                      | Merge help/error formatting options.                                   |
| `formatHelp(command?)`                   | Render program or command help.                                        |
| `formatError(error)`                     | Render an error with the configured template.                          |
| `invoke(argv?, context?)`                | Run synchronously (async handlers/resolvers throw).                    |
| `invokeAsync(argv?, context?)`           | Run and await async handlers, hooks and resolvers.                     |
| `hook()` / `hooks()`                     | Register inferred before/after hooks.                                  |

Build the program through the engine — this is the preferred entry point because
it infers the config/values types and accepts the full program options:

```ts
const program = engine.cli.program.create(
    cmd => [
        cmd('serve', {
            name: 'serve',
            description: 'Serve.',
            run: ({ config, values, context }) => {},
        }),
    ],
    {
        name: 'myapp',
        description: 'Myapp tooling.',
        version: '1.0.0',
        globalOptions: [{ flags: '--json', description: 'Print JSON.' }],
        context: { cwd: process.cwd() },
        disableColors: ({ color }) => color === false,
        writeOut: text => process.stdout.write(text),
        writeErr: text => process.stderr.write(text),
    }
);
```

`argv` defaults to `process.argv.slice(2)`, `name` defaults to `'program'`, and
`disableColors` defaults to `false`. `program.configure()` merges formatting;
`program.argv()`, `program.withContext()` and `program.output()` set the runtime
pieces.

Use the lower-level `createConfigProgram(commands, options?)` only when you
already have a command list that is not tied to an engine. It accepts the same
options and is what `engine.cli.program.create()` calls internally.

Program types: `ConfigProgram`, `ConfigProgramOptions`,
`ConfigProgramFormatOptions`, `ConfigProgramCommand`, `ConfigScopeCommand`,
`ConfigCommandBuilder`, `ConfigEngineCliProgram` and `ConfigProgramError`.

The standalone equivalent is
`generateConfigProgram(schema, { envPrefix, ... })`: it returns `CliCommand[]`
with schema-derived options. Use `engine.cli.program.create()` when you want the
typed `run({ config, values, context })` callback. See
[Generate → CLI program](/guide/config-generator/generate#cli-program).

#### `ConfigProgramError`

Invalid argv throws a `ConfigProgramError` with `code` (for example
`unknownCommand`, `unknownOption`, `missingOptionValue`, `invalidValue`,
`missingCommand`), `input` and an optional misspelling `suggestion`. Use
`format.error.messages` to override the messages and `program.formatError()` to
render one.

Options and subcommands have commander-style shorthands as well as array forms:

```ts
engine.cli.program.create(cmd => [
    cmd('serve')
        .description('Run the server.')
        .option('--json', 'Print JSON.')
        .options([
            ['--out <dir>', 'Output directory.', 'dist'],
            '--check',
            { flags: '--tag <value...>', description: 'Tags.' },
        ])
        .command('serve', 'Status.', status =>
            status
                .name('status')
                .option('--short', 'Short output.')
                .run(({ values }) => {
                    // values.short?: boolean
                })
        )
        .commands([['serve', 'Info.', info => info.name('info').run(() => {})], ['build']])
        .run(({ config, values }) => {
            // typed serve config + values
        }),
]);
```

`.options(...list)` and `.commands(...list)`/`.subcommands(...list)` accept the
same inputs spread as separate arguments. A subcommand definition may be an
already-built `CliCommand`, a `[scope, setup]` / `[scope, description, setup]`
tuple, or `{ scope, description?, setup? }`.

#### Global options

Define options once at program level and every command parses them:

```ts
const program = engine.cli.program.create(
    cmd => [
        cmd('sync').option('--check', 'Check only.').run(syncHandler),
        cmd('build').run(buildHandler),
    ],
    { globalOptions: [{ flags: '--json', description: 'Print JSON.' }] }
);

// Or after creation:
program
    .globalOption('--verbose', 'Verbose output.')
    .globalOptions([['--cwd <dir>', 'Project root.']]);
```

Commands can declare their own global options too. A subcommand only receives
the parent command's globals when it opts in with `.inherit()` (or
`inherit: true` in a command definition). Program globals always apply.

```ts
cmd('serve')
    .globalOptions([['--root <dir>', 'Project root.'], '--verbose'])
    .command('serve', status =>
        status
            .name('status')
            .inherit()
            .run(({ values }) => {
                // values.root / values.verbose are typed and parsed
            })
    )
    .run(({ values }) => {
        // the parent sees its own globals too
    });
```

Resolution order is loaded config section → env vars → explicit CLI values →
command-spec `overrides` → schema validation. Return an empty array
(`create(() => [])`) to generate one command per eligible scope;
`cliCommand: false` opts a scope out. Command metadata (`cliCommand`) supplies
`name`, `description`, `aliases`, `hidden`, `passthrough` and `args` when a
chain omits them.

`scope` is a literal union of the schema's scopes, and `run.config` is inferred
from that scope (via `ConfigOf`), so no explicit generic is needed. A
single-schema engine infers the whole schema. `ConfigProgramCommand<TConfig>`
stays exported as the base shape for custom program generators and wrappers.

The host context is generic: `ConfigProgramRunContext<TConfig, TContext =
CliCommandContext>` and `ConfigCliCommandOptions<TSchema, TContext =
CliCommandContext>` default to the minimal `{ cwd }` context. Use the callback
form to select a wider context and build commands with both `config` and
`values` inferred:

```ts
engine.cli.program.create<ToolchainCommandContext>(cmd => [
    cmd('sync')
        .description('Regenerate managed files.')
        .option({ flags: '--check', description: 'Check only.' })
        .option({ flags: '--only <tasks>', description: 'Task names.' })
        .option({ flags: '--json', description: 'Print JSON.' })
        .run(({ config, values, context }) => {
            // config: boolean | ToolchainSyncConfig
            // values.check?: boolean, values.only?: string, values.json?: boolean
            // context: ToolchainCommandContext
        }),
]);
```

Because `cmd()` is called directly, its literal `scope` and chained `option()`
calls drive the inference; `create<Context>()` only fixes the host context.
The engine itself stays schema-inferred.

Chained commands are self-contained; use `.command(scope, setup)` for typed
subcommands. Return an empty array (`create(() => [])`) to generate one command
per command-eligible scope.

#### Running a built program

A built program is commander-like: `invoke()` runs synchronously and
`invokeAsync()` awaits async handlers. `argv` defaults to
`process.argv.slice(2)` unless the program or one of its commands sets
`argv: [...]`.

```ts
const program = engine.cli.program.create(cmd => [
    cmd('sync').option({ flags: '--check', description: 'Check only.' }).run(handler),
    cmd('build').option({ flags: '--out <dir>', description: 'Output.' }).run(handler),
]);

program.argv(['sync', '--check']);
program.withContext({ cwd: process.cwd() });
await program.invokeAsync();
// or pass both explicitly:
await program.invokeAsync(['build', '--out', 'dist'], { cwd: process.cwd() });
```

Options are scoped per command: a subcommand never receives its parent's or a
sibling's flags. A sole command with no subcommands is treated as the root
command, so `invokeAsync(['--check'])` runs it without repeating the name.
Invalid argv throws a `ConfigProgramError` whose message includes a misspelling
suggestion; override the messages or render it with `program.formatError()`.

```ts
program.configure({
    error: { messages: { unknownCommand: input => `no such command: ${input}` } },
});
```

#### Help, errors, hooks and binaries

Help and error output are colourless by default. Supply colour hooks (for
example `picocolors`) to opt in; the defaults merge recursively into
subcommands and can be overridden per command, option, value, description and
usage. The default help template is `'plain'`; the default error template is
`'message'`.

```ts
import pc from 'picocolors';

program.configure({
    colors: {
        command: pc.cyan,
        option: pc.yellow,
        value: pc.green,
        description: pc.gray,
        usage: pc.bold,
    },
    options: { '--json': pc.magenta },
    commands: { sync: { colors: { command: pc.green } } },
    help: {
        template: 'box', // 'plain' (default) | 'box' | (model) => string
        box: {
            corners: { topLeft: '┌', topRight: '┐', bottomLeft: '└', bottomRight: '┘' },
            padding: 1,
        },
    },
    error: {
        // 'message' (default) | 'box' (message + stack) | custom formatter
        template: 'box',
        showStack: false,
        messageColor: pc.red,
    },
});

program.formatHelp('sync');
program.formatError(error);
```

`help.template: 'box'` wraps the commander-style content in the rounded box.
`error.template: 'box'` renders one box per error; `'message'` prints only the
message. Error formatting also exposes `messageColor`, `stackColor`,
`showStack`, `messageOnly`, `box` and `messages` (the invalid-argv message
overrides). Custom formatters receive the resolved `ConfigHelpModel` (`name`,
`description`, `usage`, `options`, `commands`, `command`) or `ConfigErrorModel`
(`errors[]`). Per-command overrides live under `commands[name]` and per-option
colors under `options['--flag']`.

Set `disableColors` when the host has its own colour switch. A function receives
the parsed program globals and the invocation context, so a `--no-color` flag
can turn every configured hook off at runtime:

```ts
const program = engine.cli.program.create(
    cmd => [
        cmd('serve', {
            name: 'serve',
            description: 'Serve.',
            run: () => {},
        }),
    ],
    {
        globalOptions: [{ flags: '--no-color', description: 'Disable colours.' }] as const,
        disableColors: ({ color }) => color === false,
    }
);
```

The callback may be async. `invoke()` requires a synchronous resolver; use
`invokeAsync()` (the normal CLI path) for async predicates.

Hooks run around the selected action and infer every declared command's
context, scope, name and runtime `values`:

```ts
program
    .hook('before', 'all', ({ name, scope, values, context }) => {})
    .hook('after', 'sync', ({ values }) => {
        // values is typed from the `sync` command's options
    })
    .hooks({ phase: 'before', target: 'build', handler: async payload => {} });
```

Set `bin` on a command to execute a relative or absolute binary instead of the
in-process handler; the arguments after the command name are forwarded verbatim.

```ts
cmd('deploy')
    .bin('./scripts/deploy.mjs')
    .run(() => {});
```

The same inference applies to `configCliCommand({ options: [...] })`: its
`run`/`parse` values are typed from the extra runtime options, while
schema-derived values remain addressable through the index signature.

### Schema metadata for CLI

```ts
const serveConfig = z.object({
    port: z
        .number()
        .default(3000)
        .meta({
            cli: { short: 'p', description: 'HTTP port.' },
        }),
    aliases: z
        .boolean()
        .default(true)
        .meta({
            cli: { flag: '--no-aliases', type: 'boolean', description: 'Skip aliases.' },
        }),
    internal: z.string().meta({ cli: false }), // never a generated flag
    format: z.union([z.boolean(), z.object({ fix: z.boolean(), command: z.string() })]),
});
```

`cli: false` prunes a field and its subtree from generated flags (env/types/docs
still include it). Arrays of scalars become list flags; arrays of objects,
records, maps and sets are skipped unless a field defines `cli` explicitly.
Ambiguous union paths are omitted and reported through the generator
`diagnostics`. Env exposure stays on `envName`/`envPath`; set
`envExpose: false` to keep a value CLI-only.

`configCommands` returns the library `config:*` generator commands; it does not
add commands to the `dbx` binary.

### `CliOptionDef`

`CliOptionDef` carries the config metadata a CLI builder needs:

| Field         | Purpose                                          |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `flag`        | Long flag (`--auto-aliases`).                    |
| `short`       | Optional shorthand (`-a`).                       |
| `env`         | Env var, for env-backed options.                 |
| `type`        | `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `array`, ...      |
| `description` | Config description.                              |
| `default`     | Stringified default.                             |
| `required`    | Config value is required.                        |
| `multiple`    | Repeated occurrences collect into an array.      |
| `choices`     | Allowed enum values, when available.             |
| `hidden`      | Registered but omitted from generated docs.      |
| `scope`       | Config scope.                                    |
| `path`        | Dotted config path (`auto.aliases`).             |
| `parse`       | Coerce one raw CLI string into the config value. |

## Root helpers

```ts
import { findProjectRoot, monorepoRoot } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

findProjectRoot(process.cwd()); // nearest project root
monorepoRoot(process.cwd()); // nearest workspace root
```

## Types

All types can be found at
[packages/config/src/types](https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/tree/main/packages/config/src/types).

# Configuration guide

A project is configured in one of two ways:

* the recommended `dbx()` **Vite plugin** in `vite.config.*` (config inline, no
  `dbx.config.*` needed), or
* a standalone `dbx.config.ts` when the project does not use Vite.

Both can be combined: `dbx.config.*` is the base and the plugin options merge on
top. The `@deltabox/toolchain` settings live under the `toolchain` key:

```ts [dbx.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@deltabox/toolchain';

export default defineConfig({
    toolchain: {
        project: {
            type: 'monorepo-root',
            name: 'myapp',
            scope: '@org',
        },
        ci: {
            ci: true,
            changelog: {
                branches: { main: 'main', dev: 'dev' },
                commitlint: { scopes: ['api', 'web', 'deps'] },
            },
        },
        tsconfig: { refs: true },
        fmt: { vscode: true, oxc: { semi: true, singleQuote: true } },
        lint: { oxc: { ignorePatterns: ['dist/**'] } },
        vite: {
            test: { include: ['src/**/*.test.ts'] },
        },
        watch: { debounce: 150 },
    },
});
```

A `dbx.config.ts` can also host other dbx concerns alongside the `toolchain`
section.

Each section has its own guide: [Project](/guide/project), [CI +
Changelog](/guide/changelog/), [tsconfig](/guide/tsconfig),
[Formatting & linting](/guide/formatting),
[Vite+](/guide/vite), [Watch](/guide/watch), [Logger](/guide/logger) and
[Providers](/guide/providers).

## Where to start

* [Opt-in by presence](/guide/config/opt-in-by-presence) — which sections run, and
  how nested sections like `ci.changelog` and the individual workflows opt in.
* [Nested configs](/guide/config/nested-configs) — how a workspace config merges
  over its root.
* [`defineConfig`](/guide/config/defineconfig) — object, promise or callback.
* [Config file names](/guide/config/config-file-names) — the file names the
  loader probes.
* [Loader](/guide/config/loader) — the `toolchain.loader` tsconfig options,
  path aliases, `.js` → `.ts` imports and examples.
* [Hooks](/guide/config/hooks) — lifecycle hooks in a `.ts`/`.js` config.
* [Logging](/guide/config/logging) — the logger section and CLI overrides.
* [Providers](/guide/config/providers) — provider passthrough colour settings.
* [Vite+](/guide/config/vite) — the full Vite+ config and the generated shim.
* [Programmatic API](/guide/config/programmatic-api) — load + sync from code.

The generated, exhaustive section reference is [dbx.config](/config/reference).
