# Vite+

There are two ways to use dbx with Vite:

* **Plugin mode (recommended):** put the toolchain config inline in the `dbx()`
  Vite plugin inside `vite.config.*`. No `dbx.config.*` is required, and dbx
  never manages `vite.config.*` because the plugin lives there.
* **Config mode:** keep the whole Vite+ config in `dbx.config.*` under
  `toolchain.vite`, and let `dbx sync` write a thin `vite.config.ts` shim.

Both can be combined: a `dbx.config.*` provides shared config and the plugin
options are merged on top.

## Vite+ as the local CLI

Install `vite-plus` as a dev dependency and let it provide Vite, Vitest, Oxfmt,
Oxlint, Rolldown and tsdown. Do not add those packages separately. On Yarn, add
`resolutions` so every dependency resolves the copies Vite+ bundles:

```json [package.json]
{
    "resolutions": {
        "vite": "npm:@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core@<core-version>",
        "vitest": "<vitest-version>"
    }
}
```

Run `vp toolchain vite-plus-core` and `vp toolchain vitest` to get the exact
versions. Without the Vitest pin, a dependency or workspace package can pull a
different Vitest and split its internals (mocks, `expect`, runner state). Use
`vp` in the package scripts (`vp dev`, `vp build`, `vp test`, `vp check`,
`vp pack`) so contributors only need the project-local CLI; a global `vp`
delegates to the same installed version.

## Plugin mode

```ts [vite.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from 'vite-plus'; // or 'vite' for plain Vite

import { dbx } from '@deltabox/toolchain/vite';

export default defineConfig({
    plugins: [
        dbx({
            toolchain: {
                project: { name: 'my-app', scope: '@org' },
                fmt: { oxc: true },
                lint: { oxc: true },
                ci: { sync: true },
                changelog: { preset: 'conventional' },
            },
        }),
    ],
    // your usual Vite config
});
```

The plugin carries the config inline and the dbx CLI (sync, projects, watch and
the VS Code extension) reads it back from `vite.config.*`. The plugin also
derives the Vite options from the dbx sections:

| dbx section | Vite option                            |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `logger`    | `logLevel` / `customLogger`            |
| `watch`     | `server.watch` (the `exclude` globs)   |
| `fmt`       | Vite+ `fmt` (only on a Vite+ project)  |
| `lint`      | Vite+ `lint` (only on a Vite+ project) |

The `vite` section is deliberately omitted from the plugin options: the Vite
config is the user config in plugin mode. Vite+ keys are only added when the
project declares `vite-plus`; a pure Vite project gets only standard Vite
options. Vite+ CLI passthroughs (`dbx vite:*`) are refused unless Vite+ is
installed/detected.

`dbx sync` runs before the dev server/build (or `dbx sync --check` in CI) and
re-syncs when `vite.config.*`, `dbx.config.*` or a tsconfig input changes.

Builtin scaffolds (`dbx create`, `dbx project:init`, `dbx project:init:workspace`)
use plugin mode: they generate a `vite.config.*` with `dbx({ toolchain })`,
Vitest (`test`) and Vite+ tasks (`run.tasks`) instead of a `dbx.config.*`. The
scaffolded packages depend on `vite-plus` and use `vp` for build/test, so no
separate `vitest` or `tsdown` dependency is written.

## Config mode

The `vite` section holds the **entire Vite+ configuration**. Every key is passed
through verbatim to Vite+, so `dbx.config.*` stays the only hand-authored root
config; `dbx sync` writes a thin root `vite.config.ts` that resolves it at load
time.

```ts [dbx.config.ts]
export default defineConfig({
    toolchain: {
        vite: {
            fmt: { semi: true, singleQuote: true },
            lint: { ignorePatterns: ['dist/**'] },
            test: { include: ['src/**/*.test.ts'], environment: 'node' },
            run: { tasks: { build: { command: 'vp pack' } } },
        },
    },
});
```

The section is typed as Vite+'s own config (`ToolchainViteConfig` = Vite's
`UserConfig` as augmented by Vite+), so the whole Vite+ surface autocompletes in
`dbx.config.ts`.

## The generated shim

`dbx sync` writes a fixed `vite.config.ts`:

```ts [vite.config.ts]
// Generated by @deltabox/toolchain.
import { defineConfig, type ViteUserConfig } from 'vite-plus';

import { resolveVite } from '@deltabox/toolchain/vite';

export default defineConfig(resolveVite<ViteUserConfig>({ cwd: import.meta.dirname }));
```

The shim imports `defineConfig` from whichever Vite package the project installs
— `vite` or `vite-plus` (detected from `package.json`, walking up so a hoisted
workspace dependency is found). For a plain `vite` project it imports
`defineConfig, type UserConfig` from `vite` and calls `resolveVite<UserConfig>`,
so the same shim type-checks against both.

`resolveVite(options?)` resolves the **same-directory** `dbx.config.*` (so a
nested workspace `vite.config.ts` uses its own config), or the `toolchain` you
pass, then returns `toolchain.vite`. You can also pass inline overrides with
`resolveVite({ vite: { ... } })`, which are deep-merged over the loaded section.
The file never drifts, because the real config stays in `dbx.config.*`.

The root shim must live at the **root**: `vp run`, `vp check` and `vp staged` do
not accept `--config`, so the shim has to be the file Vite+ loads.

## Options

| Option   | Type                | Default | Description                                     |
| -------- | ------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `config` | `boolean \| string` | `true`  | Write the managed shim; a string sets its path. |

Everything else under `vite` is Vite+ config (plugins, `test`, `lint`, `fmt`,
`run.tasks`, ...). `vite.fmt` / `vite.lint` override `toolchain.fmt.oxc` /
`toolchain.lint.oxc` (deep merge). `fmt: true` / `lint: true` use the shared
`DEFAULT_FMT_RULES` / `DEFAULT_LINT_RULES`; an options object is merged over
them. Their ignore lists are exported as `DEFAULT_FMT_IGNORE_PATTERNS` /
`DEFAULT_LINT_IGNORE_PATTERNS` (both layered over `DEFAULT_IGNORE_PATTERNS`)
from `@deltabox/toolchain` and `@deltabox/toolchain/shared`, so you can extend
them instead of repeating the defaults. Import sorting is part of those defaults:
`sortImports` gets a `workspace` custom group resolved from every dbx project
(see `resolveFmtCustomGroups`), so workspace packages do not need manual groups.
Set `vite: { config: false }` to leave a hand-written
`vite.config.ts` alone (the section is still read for provider colouring and the
`dbx` provider passthrough). `config: 'config/vite.custom.ts'` writes the shim
there instead (relative to the project, or an absolute path inside it).

## Nested workspaces

`vite` is **never inherited**. A workspace with no `vite` section keeps its
hand-written `vite.config.*` untouched; `dbx sync` only writes a shim when the
project declares `vite` itself. Declare the settings the workspace needs in its
own config:

```ts [packages/web/dbx.config.ts]
export default defineConfig({
    toolchain: {
        vite: {
            shim: 'static',
            resolve: { tsconfigPaths: true },
            run: { tasks: { build: { command: 'vp pack' } } },
        },
    },
});
```

`vite.fmt` / `vite.lint` are the exception: when the workspace opts into `fmt` /
`lint`, they are hoisted into the top-level `fmt.oxc` / `lint.oxc` before
inheritance, so shared formatting still flows down.

Vite+ recommends one root `fmt` / `lint` block with `overrides` for per-package
rules; per-workspace formatter/linter blocks are not applied by `vp check`, so
prefer the root `fmt.oxc.overrides` / `lint.oxc.overrides` (see the
[Monorepo guide](/guide/monorepo#shared-formatting-and-linting)).

## Keep the shim out of Oxfmt

Add the shim to `vite.fmt.ignorePatterns`, otherwise `vp fmt` rewrites the
generated file and `dbx sync --check` reports drift:

```ts
vite: {
    fmt: {
        ignorePatterns: ['/vite.config.ts'];
    }
}
```

In a monorepo, put `**/vite.config.ts` on the **root** top-level `fmt.oxc`
config so every workspace shim is covered (an `ignorePatterns` array in a
workspace replaces the root's list). `dbx migrate --from vite` adds the ignore
for you (see [Migrations](/guide/migrations/#vite-config)).

When `fmt` / `lint` are defined, `dbx sync` also writes `.oxfmtrc.json` /
`.oxlintrc.json` for the Oxc VS Code extension. They are root-only unless a
workspace config defines its own `fmt` / `lint`.

## Commands

Vite+ commands are reachable directly or through the `vite` namespace, and are
registered as a provider (see [Providers](/guide/providers)):

```sh
dbx fmt                 # the active formatter (vp fmt when Oxc)
dbx run -r build        # forwards to `vp run -r build`
dbx vite dev            # explicit namespace (always works)
dbx vite:build          # named alias for `vp build`
```

A bare `dbx <command>` is forwarded to Vite+ when the name (or a Vite+ alias)
matches — built-in commands win, so `dbx migrate` stays the toolchain's
migration. `dbx fmt` / `dbx lint` route to the configured/discovered
Biome/Prettier/Dprint/ESLint tool, and keep the `vp` passthrough when the active
tool is Oxc (see [Formatting & linting](/guide/formatting#running-the-active-tool)).

## Programmatic API

```ts
import {
    resolveVite,
    renderViteConfig,
    viteConfigObject,
    viteProvider,
    viteSyncTask,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain/vite';
```

| Export                         | Description                                                                       |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `resolveVite(options?)`        | Resolve `toolchain.vite` (or a passed `toolchain`), with inline `vite` overrides. |
| `detectViteSpecifier(cwd)`     | Which package (`vite` / `vite-plus`) the project has, for the shim import.        |
| `renderViteConfig(specifier?)` | The managed `vite.config.ts` shim source (defaults to `vite-plus`).               |
| `viteConfigObject(config?)`    | The `vite` section without the toolchain opt-out `config`.                        |
| `viteSyncTask()`               | The sync task (writes the shim).                                                  |
| `viteProvider()`               | The Vite+ provider descriptor.                                                    |

See [Configuration](/guide/config/vite) for the `dbx.config` integration and the
[Providers](/guide/providers) guide for the passthrough commands.

url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/vite-plugin.md
---
# Vite plugin

`@deltabox/toolchain` ships the `dbx()` Vite/Vite+ plugin. It carries the whole
toolchain config inline, so a Vite project does not need a `dbx.config.*`, and it
runs `dbx sync` before dev/build (or `dbx sync --check` in CI).

> The plugin is published from the **`@deltabox/toolchain/vite`** subpath. The
> standalone `vite-plugin-dbx` package is not published yet, so import
> `@deltabox/toolchain/vite` (not `vite-plugin-dbx`) until it ships.

## Install

```sh
yarn add -D @deltabox/toolchain
```

A Vite+ project also needs `vite-plus` (which provides `vp`, Vite, Vitest, Oxfmt
and Oxlint); see [Vite+](/guide/vite).

## Use

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite-plus'; // or 'vite'

import { dbx, DBX_TASKS } from '@deltabox/toolchain/vite';

export default defineConfig({
    plugins: [
        dbx({
            toolchain: {
                project: { name: 'my-app', scope: '@org' },
                fmt: true,
                lint: true,
                // ...any other dbx sections
            },
        }),
    ],
    run: { tasks: { ...DBX_TASKS } },
});
```

## What it does

* Loads the inline `toolchain` config (merged over a nearby `dbx.config.*` when
  one exists).
* Runs `dbx sync` before the dev server / build, or `dbx sync --check` when `CI`
  is set.
* Re-syncs when a dbx input file changes in watch mode.
* Derives Vite options from the dbx sections: `logger` → `logLevel` /
  `customLogger`, `watch` → `server.watch`, and `fmt` / `lint` → the Vite+
  formatter/linter (only when `vite-plus` is installed).
* Exposes `DBX_TASKS` (`dbx:sync`, `dbx:check`) for `run.tasks` / `vp run`.

In a **workspace**, leave `fmt` and `lint` out of the plugin config: the root
`vite.config.*` owns them and Vite+ applies the root options to the workspace.
`fmt: true` / `lint: true` there would select the shared defaults instead.

See [Vite+](/guide/vite) for the full Vite+ integration, the Vite+ provider and
the `toolchain.vite` options, and the [configuration
reference](/config/reference) for every section.

---

url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/vscode.md

# VS Code extension

This VS Code extension provides a sidebar for managing projects.

## Install

Download from the [Visual Studio Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=deltabox.toolchain-vscode).

or through the CLI:

```sh
code --install-extension deltabox.toolchain-vscode
```

## Commands

| Command                                                   | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sync all / active / selected                              | Run `dbx sync --recursive`, which walks every managed project in dependency order (nested workspaces included). Configless projects are skipped unless `deltabox.toolchain.manageConfigless` is enabled. |
| Check sync                                                | `sync --check` across the workspace.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Sync tsconfig                                             | Run `dbx sync --only tsconfig` (refresh aliases/references after builds).                                                                                                                                |
| Format project                                            | Run `dbx fmt` with the formatter detected/configured for the project (Oxfmt/Vite+, Prettier, Biome, dprint or standalone Oxc).                                                                           |
| Lint project                                              | Run `dbx lint` with the linter detected/configured for the project (Oxlint/Vite+, ESLint or Biome).                                                                                                      |
| Manage tsconfig...                                        | Auto-wire the root workspaces tsconfig paths/references (`dbx tsconfig`).                                                                                                                                |
| Scaffold project                                          | Single project, monorepo root (with/without example), workspace, or **From template...**.                                                                                                                |
| Generate configs / Generate config                        | Run `project:config` for missing configs (or for one project), or refresh only the project graph; picks TS/JS.                                                                                           |
| Migrate tooling...                                        | Migrate Biome/Prettier/Dprint/ESLint/Oxc/vite config to the toolchain (`dbx migrate`).                                                                                                                   |
| Run workflow                                              | Trigger generated workflows with their vendor CLI (`gh`/`glab`/`az`).                                                                                                                                    |
| Run Vite+ command...                                      | QuickPick over the Vite+ provider commands, run in a terminal.                                                                                                                                           |
| Create Vite+ project...                                   | `vp create` in a terminal.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Install MCP server + skill...                             | `dbx mcp:install` with a provider picker (Claude, Codex, VS Code, OpenCode, Pi or a custom directory).                                                                                                   |
| List MCP installations                                    | `dbx mcp:list` — show where the MCP server + skill are installed.                                                                                                                                        |
| Generate changelog                                        | Run `dbx changelog` in the selected project.                                                                                                                                                             |
| Clean build artifacts                                     | Remove `dist/` and `*.tsbuildinfo` (`dbx cleanup`).                                                                                                                                                      |
| Add provider... / Refresh providers                       | Register a custom provider (project or global registry) and reload the provider list.                                                                                                                    |
| Run command...                                            | Run a provider command (`dbx <command>`) in a terminal (provider tree context menu).                                                                                                                     |
| Add template... / Remove template...                      | `template:init --add` / `template:list --registry` + `template:remove`.                                                                                                                                  |
| Add template... / Remove template source...               | Registry actions: add a template source or drop one while keeping the files; **Refresh templates** reloads the list.                                                                                     |
| Create from template...                                   | `dbx create --template <id>` (terminal for online templates; `--online` is added automatically for online sources).                                                                                      |
| New registry... / Remove registry... / Refresh registries | Manage the provider/template registry search paths and reload the **Registries** view.                                                                                                                   |
| Choose dbx source... / Select dbx version...              | Pick the project's `dbx` or the bundled CLI, and pin the toolchain version.                                                                                                                              |
| Refresh projects / Refresh files                          | Rediscover the project graph / reload the **Managed Files** view.                                                                                                                                        |
| Show all actions                                          | Open the searchable action palette (see [Actions](#actions)).                                                                                                                                            |
| Reset tooling                                             | Remove generated files / manifest / config.                                                                                                                                                              |
| Toggle auto-sync                                          | Enable/disable sync-on-change.                                                                                                                                                                           |

Interactive commands (the dev server, `vp create`, online scaffolding) run in an
integrated terminal at the project root; everything else runs in the output
channel.

**Format project** and **Lint project** are generic toolchain commands, not
Vite+ commands: they run `dbx fmt` / `dbx lint`, which route to the
detected/configured formatter and linter. A project using Prettier, ESLint,
Biome, dprint or standalone Oxc gets the same actions as a Vite+ project (the
`vp` passthrough is only used when Oxc is backed by `vite-plus`).

Tree context menus also expose scoped commands that are hidden from the Command
Palette: **Sync this project**, **Go to project**, **Run the project's Vite+
command**, **Remove provider**, **Copy provider id**, **Create from template**,
**Show template info**, **Copy template id**, and the registry item actions
(**Open registry**, **Add new registry**, **Remove registry**).

## Project menu

Every project card (and every project in the **Projects** tree) exposes the same
actions, scoped to that project:

* **Sync** / **Check sync** — regenerate / verify the project's managed files.
* **Generate config** — write a `dbx.config.*` (TS/JS), or refresh only the project graph.
* **Run workflow...** — trigger one of the project's generated workflows. The picker
  lists every enabled workflow with its provider and path, and dispatches it
  through the matching vendor CLI (`gh`, `glab` or `az`).
* **Run Vite+ command...** — run a `vp` command in that project.
* **Reset tooling...** — remove the generated files + manifest, or everything
  including the config.
* **Go to project** — reveal the project in the Explorer.

## File Explorer decorations and project reveal

Every file recorded in a project's `.dbx/toolchain/manifest.json` gets a `dbx`
badge and the contributed blue label color in the File Explorer. The decoration
refreshes after a sync (and from **Refresh files**), and can be turned off with
`deltabox.toolchain.decorateManagedFiles`. VS Code has no contribution point
that overrides a single file's icon inside the active file icon theme, so the
badge plus label color is the supported marker; changing the icon itself would
require switching the whole workbench icon theme.

Switching the active editor selects the deepest project that owns the file in
the **Projects** view and expands its workspace group. Files outside every
project are ignored, the reveal never takes focus, and the listener is disposed
with the extension.

## Providers, templates and Vite+ in the editor

The **Providers** and **Templates** views read `dbx providers --json` and `dbx template:list --json`, so adding one surfaces it in the UI automatically.

### Plugin mode

A project configured through the `dbx()` Vite plugin (rather than a
`dbx.config.*`) is detected automatically: the Projects view shows it as
`plugin`, sync stays enabled, and auto-sync watches `vite.config.*`. The
extension never manages `vite.config.*` in plugin mode — the CLI's `vite` sync
task skips it, and config generation skips projects that already have the
plugin.

Vite+ commands are only enabled when Vite+ is detected for the project. When it
is not, the provider and its commands are greyed out (`available: false` in
`dbx providers --json`) and the extension refuses to run them, while plain Vite
projects keep working normally.

### Add provider...

Writes a custom provider to the default project registry (`.dbx/toolchain/.registry/providers/providers.json`) or the global
`~/.dbx/toolchain/.registry/providers/` when you choose the global scope, which
`toolchainProviders()` merges with the built-ins, so a registered provider's
commands also become `dbx` commands (`dbx <command>`), runnable from the view.

Provider search paths can also be added with the **Registries** view; the
`deltabox.providerRegistrySearchPaths` setting mirrors them globally.

### Add template...

Runs `template:init --add` and asks whether to add the template to the **global** registry (yes by default), so it is available in every
project.

See [Global templates](/guide/templates#global-templates).

The
`deltabox.registrySearchPaths` setting controls the global search paths and is
kept in sync with the CLI config.

### Remove template source...

Runs `template:list --registry` + `template:remove`.

The **Registries** view (below **Templates**) shows the detected provider and
template registries as **Providers** / **Templates** roots.

Each item has **Open registry** (the folder in the explorer, or the website for remote URLs), **Add new registry** and **Remove registry** (it only drops the path, keeping the files).

The title bar's **New registry...** / **Remove registry...** actions add or remove
search paths for either kind, asking whether they are global or project-scoped.

Remote registries are `http(s)` JSON registries: template registries accept
`{ sources }` or an array of sources; provider registries accept
`{ providers }` or an array of provider descriptors.

### Create from template...

Prompts for the template's inputs and actions (see
[Templates](/guide/templates)) before running `dbx create`. Scaffolding also asks
for a package manager (`yarn` default).

The Home view links to this documentation with **Need help? Go to documentation**.

## Actions

The **Actions** view (below **Projects**) lists every dbx action grouped by area
(Changelog, CI, Cleanup, MCP, Migrate, Pack, Project, Providers, Registries,
Sync, Templates, Tools). Groups are collapsed by default and sorted ascending;
expanding one shows its actions sorted by name. Selecting an action runs its VS
Code command directly.

The Home view's **More actions...** button opens the same list as a searchable,
paged QuickPick. Navigation entries (`Go back`, `Next page (n/m)`) are rendered
before the real choices, and every prompt-based dbx flow (scaffolding, template
pickers, ...) uses the same paging factory. Actions only delegate to their own VS
Code command; the palette itself never shells out.

## Auto-sync

The Home view shows the current state as a clickable **Auto-sync enabled** /
**Auto-sync paused** button (the same secondary style as the other quick
actions). Opening it lists the global and workspace scopes independently, so a
global value and a workspace value can disagree:

* **Enable/Disable (global)** writes `deltabox.toolchain.enabled` at the global
  VS Code scope and mirrors the value into the CLI global store
  (`~/.dbx/toolchain/cli/config.json`, via `dbx enable/disable --global`).
* **Enable/Disable (workspace)** writes `.vscode/settings.json` through the
  workspace configuration target (via `dbx enable/disable --workspace`).

A project's `toolchain.enabled` config takes precedence over both settings. The
extension resolves it through the project's CLI (`dbx enabled --json`), so a
disabled config keeps auto-sync off even when the VS Code setting is on.

Auto-sync watches input files only. The extension asks the CLI
(`dbx watch --list --json`) for the concrete, project-graph-resolved files:
every `dbx.config.*` plus each enabled project's `tsconfig.baseFile`,
`tsconfig.defaultFile` and the root `tsconfig.rootFile`. Custom file names are
honoured, nested configs can disable or override their own tsconfig section, and
the list is refreshed whenever a `dbx.config.*` changes (and after each sync).

Each resolved pattern is scoped to its own workspace root (and a concrete
nested file is watched from its own directory), so a same-named file in another
workspace folder or an ancestor can never trigger this root's sync, and VS Code
does not install a recursive watcher over the whole root (which can hold
`node_modules` handles during a package-manager link step on Windows). Only the
root whose input changed is synced. Setting `deltabox.toolchain.watch`
explicitly replaces the resolved inputs; user globs are matched across every
workspace folder, absolute/ancestor globs are ignored, and an empty list
disables watching.

Generated outputs are never watched. The scheduler debounces bursts, allows one sync at a time, queues at most one follow-up, and suppresses events briefly after a run.

When a sync finds no workspace tsconfig files while `tsconfig.refs`/`tsconfig.composite` are on (or a `tsconfig.workspaces.json` is present), the extension surfaces the CLI's warning as a notification (once per session) with a **Show output** action.

When removing a section stops managing a file that dbx created, the sync
notification lists the removed relative paths and offers **Restore** (write the
previous content back) or **Close**. A file that existed before dbx first managed
it is **adopted**: it is unmanaged but never deleted.

The **Managed Files** view also shows a **Workflow conflicts** group for
hand-written workflows dbx left untouched (the manifest's `workflowConflicts`).
Each item names the config key to opt out with, and opens the existing file.

## Settings

| Setting                                              | Default         | Description                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deltabox.toolchain.enabled`                         | `true`          | Auto sync on watched changes. A project's `toolchain.enabled` config takes precedence.                     |
| `deltabox.toolchain.debounce`                        | `300`           | Debounce (ms) before a sync.                                                                               |
| `deltabox.toolchain.command`                         | `sync`          | The command to run on change.                                                                              |
| `deltabox.toolchain.manageConfigless`                | `false`         | Manage projects without their own `dbx.config.*` (passes `--configless` to sync/watch).                    |
| `deltabox.toolchain.containerizeTemplates`           | `false`         | Generate Docker artifacts when scaffolding a new project (also prompted per create).                       |
| `deltabox.toolchain.formatManagedFiles`              | `true`          | Format the managed files written by `dbx sync` (adds `--no-format` when disabled).                         |
| `deltabox.toolchain.formatManagedFilesFix`           | `true`          | Rewrite managed files when formatting instead of check mode (adds `--no-format-fix` when disabled).        |
| `deltabox.toolchain.formatManagedFilesCommand`       | `""`            | Override the managed-file formatter command (`{files}` expands to the files). Empty = auto-detect.         |
| `deltabox.toolchain.formatManagedFilesExclude`       | `[]`            | Managed files to leave unformatted (globs; passed to `dbx sync --format-exclude`).                         |
| `deltabox.toolchain.enableFormatImportGroupDefaults` | `true`          | Add the resolved workspace `sortImports` custom group when syncing; set `false` to manage groups yourself. |
| `deltabox.toolchain.decorateManagedFiles`            | `true`          | Show a `dbx` badge and blue label color on files recorded in the project manifests.                        |
| `deltabox.toolchain.watch`                           | `[]` (resolved) | Inputs that trigger a sync (empty = resolved from the config).                                             |
| `deltabox.toolchain.version`                         | `""` (auto)     | Pin the `@deltabox/toolchain` version this workspace runs.                                                 |
| `deltabox.registrySearchPaths`                       | `[]`            | Template registry search paths (dirs or `http(s)` URLs).                                                   |
| `deltabox.providerRegistrySearchPaths`               | `[]`            | Provider registry search paths (JSON files/dirs/URLs).                                                     |

`deltabox.toolchain.enableFormatImportGroupDefaults` (default `true`) adds the
resolved `workspace` group to Oxfmt's `sortImports.customGroups` when the
extension syncs or generates configs. Set it to `false` in user or workspace
settings to keep full control of the import groups. The extension passes the
effective value to the CLI; direct CLI runs and Vite+ configs also honour the
workspace-scoped `.vscode/settings.json` value.

When a workspace has its own `@deltabox/toolchain` whose version differs from the
extension's bundled CLI, the extension asks which to run and shows both detected
versions. **Select dbx version...** pins a version in the project's
`.vscode/settings.json` (like TypeScript's version picker); it runs that version
via `npx` unless the project already installs it.

Project lookup follows the repository boundary: from the open folder (and every
workspace root in a multi-root workspace) the extension walks up to the nearest
`.git`, so a toolchain hoisted to the monorepo root is found even when a nested
workspace package is opened as the folder. The project's own `dbx` stays the
default; the bundled CLI is only the fallback.

## Command palette

Search for `deltabox:` to find:

* **Sync active project** / **Sync selected projects** / **Sync all projects**
* **Check sync**
* **Sync tsconfig**
* **Manage tsconfig...**

* **Generate configs...** / **Generate config...**

* **Install MCP server + skill...**

* **Show all actions**
* **Reset tooling...**
* **Toggle auto-sync**

The project and tree context menus add scoped commands that are intentionally
hidden from the palette (sync this project, go to project, run the project's
Vite+ command, remove/copy a provider, template info/copy id, and the registry
item actions).

# Providers

A **provider** is an external toolchain exposed through `dbx`: its CLI,
the programmatic API and the VS Code extension. Providers contribute namespaced
commands and a descriptor the editor reads over `dbx providers --json`.

## List providers

```sh
dbx providers          # table
dbx providers --json   # descriptor (id, binary, commands, actions)
```

## Vite+ (`vite-plus`)

The bundled provider wraps the `vp` binary — the unified Vite / Vitest / Oxlint /
Oxfmt / Rolldown / tsdown toolchain.

### Resolution

`dbx vite:*` resolves `vp` in this order:

1. the project-local shim (`node_modules/.bin/vp`),
2. a global `vp` on `PATH`,
3. `npx --yes vite-plus`.

### Generic passthrough

```sh
dbx vite dev
dbx vite build
dbx vite add zod
dbx vite check
```

Everything after `vite` is forwarded verbatim to `vp`, so all Vite+ commands and
flags are reachable. A bare `dbx <command>` whose name is a Vite+ command (or a
Vite+ alias) is forwarded too, so `dbx fmt` / `dbx run -r build` need no `vite`
namespace — built-in commands win (`dbx migrate` stays the toolchain's).

### Colour

Provider output keeps `vp`'s own colours, but follows the logger's colour state.
The global `--no-color` flag turns provider colour off, and the `providers`
section can opt out on its own even on a colour terminal:

```ts [dbx.config.ts]
export default defineConfig({
    toolchain: {
        providers: { color: false },
    },
});
```

When colour is off, `dbx` runs `vp` with `NO_COLOR=1` and `FORCE_COLOR=0` so the
wrapped process emits plain output. Leave the section unset to let `vp` detect
colour from its own terminal.

### Named commands

Every catalogued subcommand is also available as a first-class command for
discovery + the editor:

```
vite:create  vite:migrate  vite:dev  vite:check  vite:lint  vite:fmt  vite:test
vite:build   vite:pack     vite:run  vite:add    vite:remove vite:update ...
vite:toolchain vite:upgrade vite:implode
```

### Programmatic

```ts
import {
    resolveVp,
    runVp,
    hasVp,
    vpVersion,
    describeVp,
    resolveVpCommand,
    viteCommandName,
    VP_COMMANDS,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain/vite';

if (hasVp(process.cwd())) {
    await runVp(['check'], { cwd: process.cwd() });
}
```

| Export                                 | Description                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `resolveVp(cwd?)`                      | Resolve the `vp` invocation (`{ exe, args, source }`).                      |
| `hasVp(cwd?)`                          | Whether a local/global `vp` is available (no `npx` fallback).               |
| `runVp(args, options?)`                | Run `vp`, streaming output or `mode: 'capture'`; never exits the host.      |
| `vpVersion(cwd?)` / `describeVp(cwd?)` | The `vp --version` output / a one-line resolution description.              |
| `which(bin)`                           | Find an executable on `PATH` (resolves `PATHEXT` on Windows).               |
| `resolveVpCommand(name)`               | Resolve a subcommand **or alias** to its canonical name (`i` -> `install`). |
| `viteCommandName(name)`                | The `dbx` command name for a `vp` subcommand (`dev` -> `vite:dev`).         |
| `VP_COMMANDS`                          | The `vp` command catalog that drives the CLI + the provider descriptor.     |

```ts
// A bare `dbx <command>` falls through to `vite` when it names a Vite+ command.
resolveVpCommand('fmt'); // 'fmt'
viteCommandName('fmt'); // 'vite:fmt'
```

### Use dbx from Vite+

Vite+ consumers can drive dbx from `vite.config.ts`, so a Vite+-only project
still gets dbx's generated/managed files:

```ts [vite.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from 'vite-plus';

import { dbx, DBX_TASKS } from '@deltabox/toolchain/vite';

export default defineConfig({
    plugins: [dbx()],
    run: { tasks: { ...DBX_TASKS } },
    // your usual Vite / Vite+ config
});
```

* The `dbx()` plugin runs `dbx sync` before the dev server / build, or
  `dbx sync --check` in CI (which fails the build when generated files are out of
  date), and re-syncs when a `dbx.config.*` / `tsconfig.*.json` input changes.
* The plugin resolves the `dbx` binary from the project first: the local
  `node_modules/.bin/dbx`, then the project's own `@deltabox/toolchain` bin. A
  global `dbx` on `PATH` is used **only when the project doesn't pin the
  toolchain at all** — otherwise it's skipped (with a warning) in favour of
  `npx @deltabox/toolchain@<pinned>`. That way a stale global install can never
  run and silently revert the project's generated files.
* `run: { tasks: { ...DBX_TASKS } }` also exposes `vp run dbx:sync` /
  `vp run dbx:check`. Vite+ reads `run.tasks` from the **static** config (a
  plugin's `config` hook is ignored), so the tasks are spread in the config
  rather than added by the plugin. Drop the `run` block if you don't want them.
* Because Vite Task runs a task's `command` through a shell, `DBX_TASKS` bakes in
  the binary resolved by `resolveDbx` (the project's own, or the pinned `npx`
  fallback) rather than relying on `dbx` being on `PATH` — a missing environment
  then warns instead of silently running the wrong binary. Use `dbxTaskCommand(sub)`
  to build a task command for another subcommand.

## Other language toolchains

Providers are not JavaScript-only. A provider is just a descriptor around a CLI
binary, so the same mechanism can expose the tools a polyglot repository already
uses:

| Language  | Binary                     | Example commands                      |
| --------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Python    | `uv` (or `ruff`, `pytest`) | `dbx python:run`, `dbx python:sync`   |
| C# / .NET | `dotnet`                   | `dbx dotnet:build`, `dbx dotnet:test` |
| Java      | `mvn` / `gradle`           | `dbx maven:test`, `dbx gradle:build`  |
| Rust      | `cargo`                    | `dbx rust:build`, `dbx rust:clippy`   |
| Go        | `go`                       | `dbx go:test`, `dbx go:vet`           |

Each provider maps command names to a `binary` + `subcommand`; remaining operands
are forwarded verbatim. Register one provider per binary, or use a runner such as
`uv` or `cargo` to cover several tasks. Once registered, the commands appear in
`dbx providers`, the CLI help and the VS Code Providers view, so a polyglot repo
has one command surface even when the languages do not.

```json [.dbx/toolchain/.registry/providers/rust.json]
[
    {
        "id": "rust",
        "name": "Rust (cargo)",
        "binary": "cargo",
        "commands": [
            {
                "name": "rust:build",
                "subcommand": "build",
                "description": "Build the Rust workspace."
            },
            {
                "name": "rust:test",
                "subcommand": "test",
                "description": "Run Rust tests."
            },
            {
                "name": "rust:clippy",
                "subcommand": "clippy",
                "description": "Lint with Clippy."
            },
            {
                "name": "rust:fmt",
                "subcommand": "fmt",
                "description": "Format Rust sources."
            }
        ]
    }
]
```

## Custom providers

Providers are loaded from **search paths** (JSON files, directories of
`*.json`, or `http(s)` registry URLs). A JSON file can be an array of provider
descriptors or `{ "providers": [...] }`.

Project paths (first wins on an id clash):

* `.dbx/toolchain/.registry/providers` — the implicit default directory;
* `.dbx/toolchain/registries.json` — its `providers` array;
* `.dbx/toolchain/providers.json` — the legacy file, still read.

Global paths:

* `~/.dbx/toolchain/.registry/providers` — the default directory;
* `~/.dbx/toolchain/cli/config.json` — `providerRegistrySearchPaths`, or
  `registrySearchPaths.providers`;
* the VS Code `deltabox.providerRegistrySearchPaths` setting (kept in sync).

`toolchainProviders()` merges every local registry with the built-ins (a project
provider wins on an id clash), so a custom provider's commands become `dbx`
commands — `dbx <command.name>` forwards to `<binary> <subcommand> ...` — and it
shows up in `dbx providers` and the editor. Remote registries are fetched by
`dbx providers --json`/`loadToolchainProviders()`. Restrict them with
`toolchain.registry.providers` (`allow`/`deny` host + path globs); the same
policy applies to local registry paths:

```json [.dbx/toolchain/.registry/providers/providers.json]
[
    {
        "id": "echo",
        "name": "Echo",
        "binary": "node",
        "commands": [
            {
                "name": "echo:version",
                "subcommand": "--version",
                "description": "Print the Node version"
            }
        ]
    }
]
```

```sh
dbx registry --json                                  # list template + provider paths
dbx registry --kind providers --scope project --add ./providers
dbx registry --kind providers --scope global --add https://example.com/providers.json
```

The VS Code **Providers** view manages the registry items (**Add provider...** /
**Remove provider**), and the **Registries** view shows the provider search
paths. See [VS Code Extension](/guide/vscode).

For a rendered directory tree of a typical custom provider, template and
registry, see
[Template and registry structures](/guide/template-structures#custom-providers).

## Providers in the editor

The VS Code extension reads `providers --json` and builds its **Providers** view
and menus from it, so adding a provider surfaces it automatically. See
[VS Code Extension](/guide/vscode).
