   `vitest` and `tsdown` dev dependencies with `vite-plus`.
2. Import the Vite plugin from `@deltabox/toolchain/vite` (not
   `vite-plugin-dbx`, which is not published yet).
3. If the project uses Vite+, move `tsdown.config.*`, `vitest.config.*` and
   `turbo.json` into `vite.config.*` as `pack`, `test` and `run.tasks`.
4. Run `dbx sync --recursive` and commit the regenerated managed files.
5. Rename generated `env.d.ts` references to `dbx-env.d.ts`, and switch custom
   runtime loaders to `parseConfig` / `parseEnvConfig` / `parseCliConfig` (or
   `loadConfigAsync` for files).
6. Run `dbx sync --recursive --check`, `yarn typecheck`, `yarn lint` and your
   test suite.
7. Regenerate Docker artifacts created by v2 (or edit the `COPY` lines to list
   only files that exist) and rebuild the image once with Docker available.
8. Replace imports of the old monolithic template helper with
   `PROJECT_TEMPLATE_IDS` / `createProjectTemplateFiles`.
9. If you build a `DockerPlan` by hand, add its `installSources` (or switch to
   `resolveDockerPlan()`).
10. Re-run `dbx migrate --check` in CI; inherited workspace configs may now pass
    where v2 reported a false drift.
11. Add `--online` to any `dbx create --template` / `template:*` script that
    resolves npm/git/Vite+ sources.
12. If you use `ci.dependabot`, opt into `security` and add the
    `DBX_GITHUB_TOKEN` secret (repository admin) before the generated security
    workflow runs.
13. If you assemble a custom CLI, rebuild it with `engine.cli.program.create()`
    (or the lower-level `createConfigProgram()` for engine-agnostic command
    lists), wrap descriptors in `defineCliCommand()`, and move any `commander`
    wiring to the program runtime.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/api.md
---
# Programmatic API

Every surface the CLI and the extension use is also importable. The umbrella
package re-exports the config model + sync runner and every workspace package, so
a consumer can import the whole surface from the root or a single package through
a subpath.

## Where to start

* [Umbrella (`@deltabox/toolchain`)](/guide/api/umbrella) — the root exports and
  the namespaced packages.
* [Subpath exports](/guide/api/subpath-exports) — the per-package entry points.
* [Package reference](/guide/api/package-reference) — every package's public
  exports.
* [Logging](/guide/api/logging) — the shared logger.
* [Examples](/guide/api/examples) — short, copy-pasteable recipes.
* [Registering commands](/guide/api/registering-commands) — wire
  `CliCommand[]` onto the engine program runtime.

```ts
import { defineConfig, loadToolchainConfig, runSync, defaultSyncTasks } from '@deltabox/toolchain';

const { config, tokens, projectType } = await loadToolchainConfig(process.cwd());
await runSync({ tasks: defaultSyncTasks(), cwd: process.cwd(), config, tokens, projectType });
```

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/api/examples.md
---
# Examples

## Vite+ provider

Resolve and run the project's Vite+ CLI, or map a Vite+ command name:

```ts
import { resolveVp, runVp, resolveVpCommand, VP_COMMANDS } from '@deltabox/toolchain/vite';

await runVp(['check'], { cwd: process.cwd() });
resolveVpCommand('i'); // 'install'
```

## Migrations

Detect the migrations that apply to a project and run them:

```ts
import { detectMigrations, runMigration } from '@deltabox/toolchain/migrate';

for (const migration of detectMigrations(process.cwd())) {
    await migration.run({ cwd: process.cwd(), write: true });
}
```

## Templates

Load the available templates and scaffold one:

```ts
import { loadTemplates, scaffoldTemplate } from '@deltabox/toolchain/template';

const [template] = await loadTemplates({ cwd: process.cwd() });

if (template) {
    await scaffoldTemplate(template, {
        cwd: './out',
        tokens: { name: 'myapp' },
    });
}
```

## Providers

Read provider descriptors the way the editor does:

```ts
import { toolchainProviders } from '@deltabox/toolchain/providers';

console.log(toolchainProviders().map(provider => provider.id));
```

## Sync only the tsconfig task

Useful after a build changes package exports:

```ts
import { defaultSyncTasks, loadToolchainConfig, runSync } from '@deltabox/toolchain';

const loaded = await loadToolchainConfig(process.cwd());

await runSync({
    tasks: defaultSyncTasks(),
    only: ['tsconfig'],
    cwd: process.cwd(),
    config: loaded.config,
    tokens: loaded.tokens,
    projectType: loaded.projectType,
});
```

## Config engine

Bind a schema once, then use it to generate or parse configuration:

```ts
import { createConfigEngine, parseEnvConfig } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const engine = createConfigEngine({ schema, envPrefix: 'MYAPP_' });
const runtimeConfig = parseEnvConfig(engine.schema, process.env, {
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
});
```

## Runnable CLI program

Build a CLI from the generated config commands:

```ts
import { configCommands } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const program = engine.cli.program.create(() => configCommands({ engine }), {
    name: 'my-cli',
    globalOptions: [{ flags: '--no-color', description: 'Disable colours.' }] as const,
    disableColors: ({ color }) => color === false,
});

await program.invokeAsync(process.argv.slice(2));
```

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/api/logging.md
---
# Logging

Every toolchain message goes through one level-aware logger, rendered with
[`@clack/prompts`](https://bombshell.dev/clack) (level symbols + guide). Use it
instead of `console.log` so output stays consistent and respects the config and
the CLI flags.

| Export / member                                   | Description                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `logger`                                          | The active singleton: `raw`, `debug`, `info`, `success`, `warn`, `error`, `level`, `colors`. |
| `createLogger(options)`                           | Create an independent logger (`level`, `color`, `name`).                                     |
| `setLogConfig(section)`                           | Apply the `logger` section from the loaded config.                                           |
| `setLogOverrides(options)`                        | Apply CLI overrides (win over the config). `configureLogger` is an alias.                    |
| `getLogOverrides()` / `getLogger()`               | Read the current overrides / the active instance.                                            |
| `LOG_LEVELS` / `isLogLevel` / `normalizeLogLevel` | The valid levels, most verbose first (`debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `silent`).           |

```ts
import { createLogger, logger, setLogConfig, setLogOverrides } from '@deltabox/toolchain/shared';

setLogConfig({ level: 'debug', color: false, name: 'dbx' }); // from dbx.config.*
setLogOverrides({ level: 'warn' }); // from --log-level

logger.info('human message');
logger.success('done');
logger.error('failed');
logger.raw(JSON.stringify(payload)); // machine output: no prefix, no colour
```

Use `raw` for machine output (`--json`): it is never prefixed or decorated.
`logger.warn`/`error` write to stderr; `debug`/`info`/`success`/`raw` to stdout.
Messages that start with whitespace (indented continuations) are never prefixed.

This mirrors the [`logger` config section](/guide/config/logging) and the
`--log-level <level>` / `--no-color` [CLI flags](/guide/cli#global-flags), which
call `setLogConfig` / `setLogOverrides` under the hood.

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/api/package-reference.md
---
# Package reference

## `@deltabox/toolchain/shared`

The base layer: the config model, logging, process/string/object utilities and
the template engine.

| Export                                                                                     | Description                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defineConfig(config)`                                                                     | Identity helper for a typed `dbx.config.*` (object, promise, or sync/async callback).       |
| `sectionEnabled(section)` / `sectionConfig(section)`                                       | Opt-in-by-presence helpers for a config section.                                            |
| `resolveTokens(config)`                                                                    | Flatten a config into {{ token }} replacements.                          |
| `CONFIG_FILE_NAMES`                                                                        | The config file names the loader probes, in priority order.                                 |
| `repoSlugFromUrl(url)`                                                                     | Derive an `owner/name` slug from a repository URL.                                          |
| `findOwnCliEntry(cwd?)` / `localToolchainVersion(cwd?)` / `TOOLCHAIN_PACKAGE`              | Locate a project's own toolchain bin + pinned version (prefer them over a global `dbx`).    |
| `createLogger(options)` / `logger`                                                         | The shared logger (see [Logging](/guide/api/logging)).                                      |
| `WARNING_MAP` / `ERROR_MAP` / `warningMessage(id, values?)`                                | Central messages keyed by stable logger/suppression ids.                                    |
| `spawnCross(cmd, args, options)` / `run(cmd, args, options)`                               | Cross-platform, shell-free spawning; `timeoutMs` kills the child tree.                      |
| `killProcessTree(child)`                                                                   | Kill a child process and its descendants (Windows `taskkill /t`).                           |
| `readJsonFile` / `readJsonAt` / `toJson` / `writeJsonFile`                                 | Small JSON file helpers.                                                                    |
| `mergeJsonAt(cwd, relative, patch)`                                                        | Deep-merge a patch over an existing JSON file.                                              |
| `deepMerge` / `applyOverrides` / `isPlainObject` / `sort` / `mapValues`                    | Object utilities (including layered typed overrides).                                       |
| `defineCliCommand(command)`                                                                | Build a `CliCommand` while preserving the literal `options` tuple for typed values.         |
| `CliOptionValues<TOptions>`                                                                | The commander-style typed values produced by an option tuple.                               |
| `applyReplacements` / `applyReplacementsDeep` / `createReplacer`                           | The {{ token }} template engine (also `tokenPattern`, `extractTokens`).  |
| `DEFAULT_IGNORE_PATTERNS` / `DEFAULT_FMT_IGNORE_PATTERNS` / `DEFAULT_LINT_IGNORE_PATTERNS` | The shared build/cache ignores and the Oxfmt/Oxlint extensions.                             |
| `resolveIgnorePatterns(cwd?, options?)` / `collectGitignorePatterns(cwd?)`                 | Defaults + `exclude` + `.gitignore` resolution, and the matching helpers (`isIgnoredPath`). |
| `toYaml(value)`                                                                            | A tiny YAML emitter for the GitHub Actions subset.                                          |

The config **types** and **schemas** also live here: `ToolchainConfig`, `DbxConfig`,
`SyncTask`, `SyncContext`, `ManagedFile`, `CliCommand`, `CliOption`,
`CliOptionValues`, `CliCommandContext`, `ToolchainProvider`,
`ToolchainViteConfig` (Vite+'s config type), `Replacements`,
and the generated `config-types` / `config-schema` exports.

```ts
import { defineConfig, sectionEnabled, applyReplacements } from '@deltabox/toolchain/shared';

const text = applyReplacements('Hello {{name:world}}', { name: 'myapp' });
```

## `@deltabox/toolchain/core`

Loads `dbx.config.*`, builds the project graph and runs the sync tasks.

| Export                                                        | Description                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `loadToolchainConfig(cwd?)`                                   | Find + load the config, resolve tokens and the project type.                        |
| `findConfigFile(cwd?)`                                        | The config file path, if any.                                                       |
| `runSync(options)`                                            | Run the given `SyncTask[]` (or `only` a named subset) and return the summary.       |
| `runWatch(options)`                                           | Sync once, then watch inputs and re-sync (honours `only`).                          |
| `selectSyncTasks(tasks, only)`                                | Select tasks by name; throws on unknown names.                                      |
| `buildProjectGraph(root, options?)`                           | Discover workspace packages and their dependencies.                                 |
| `orderProjects(nodes)` / `detectPackageManager(root)`         | Dependency ordering and package-manager detection.                                  |
| `writeProjectGraph` / `readProjectGraph`                      | Persist/read `.dbx/toolchain/projects.json`.                                        |
| `selectProjects(options)`                                     | Select projects by kind/name/glob.                                                  |
| `resetToolchain(options)` / `resetProjects(options)`          | Remove generated files, the manifest and/or the config (`restore` hook runs first). |
| `vscodeSyncTask(options?)`                                    | The VS Code settings/extensions sync task.                                          |
| `resolveProjectType(cwd, config?)` / `detectProjectType(cwd)` | The project kind (`monorepo-root` / `monorepo-workspace` / `project`).              |
| `readManifest(cwd)` / `writeManifest(cwd, files)`             | The `.dbx/toolchain/manifest.json` helpers.                                         |
| `resolveFmtCustomGroups(input?)`                              | Build the `sortImports` workspace group from every dbx project (graph-based).       |

```ts
import { defaultSyncTasks, runSync, selectSyncTasks } from '@deltabox/toolchain';

await runSync({
    tasks: defaultSyncTasks(),
    only: ['tsconfig'],
    cwd,
    config,
    tokens,
});

// Or select explicitly:
const tasks = selectSyncTasks(defaultSyncTasks(), ['tsconfig']);
```

`only` implies `prune: false`, so a task subset never deletes files owned by the
tasks it skipped. Unknown task names throw.

## `@deltabox/toolchain/config`

The generic Zod/env engine (see the [Config Generator](/guide/config-generator/)
guide for the full workflow).

| Export                                                                                   | Description                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createConfigEngine(options)`                                                            | Bind a schema, env prefix, base group and root into an engine.   |
| `parseConfig` / `parseEnvConfig` / `parseCliConfig`                                      | Runtime parsers: env + CLI + overrides, validated.               |
| `loadConfig` / `loadConfigSync` / `loadConfigAsync`                                      | Discover/import a config file and parse it.                      |
| `loadEnvConfig*` / `loadCliConfig*` / `loadFileConfig*`                                  | Source-specific loader variants (Sync/Async).                    |
| `collect(schema, options?)`                                                              | Resolve env + CLI into a typed config (no overrides).            |
| `configCommands({ engine, defaults? })`                                                  | The `config:*` commands for a consumer's own CLI.                |
| `createConfigProgram(commands, options?)`                                                | Low-level program factory; prefer `engine.cli.program.create()`. |
| `generateConfigProgram(schema, options)`                                                 | Generate `CliCommand[]` from a config schema.                    |
| `ConfigProgramError`                                                                     | Invalid-argv error (`code`, `input`, optional `suggestion`).     |
| `formatGenerated(source, options?)`                                                      | Format generated output with Oxfmt (see below).                  |
| `GENERATED_FORMAT_OPTIONS`                                                               | The baseline Oxfmt options used by the generators.               |
| `parseEnvTree(env, prefix?)` / `envString` / `envInt` / `envBool` / `envList` / `envMap` | Legacy dependency-free tree accessors.                           |
| `compileZodSchema(schema)`                                                               | Compile a Zod schema for fast repeated parsing.                  |
| `envPathOf(env, prefix?)` / `metaOf(schema)`                                             | Env-name to dotted-path derivation and `.meta()` reading.        |
| `findProjectRoot(start?)` / `monorepoRoot(from?)`                                        | Walk up to the nearest `package.json`.                           |
| `generateConfigTypes` / `generateConfigEnv`                                              | Type/env generators (optional disk writes).                      |
| `generateConfigMarkdown` / `generateCliOptions`                                          | Markdown/CLI generators (optional disk writes).                  |
| `generateCliDocs(commands, options?)`                                                    | A CLI reference from `CliCommand` descriptors.                   |
| `generateConfigJsonSchema` / `generateJsonSchemaFile`                                    | JSON Schema generation.                                          |
| `normalizeJsonSchemaMetadata(node)`                                                      | Normalize Zod JSON Schema metadata for editor schemas.           |
| `generateEnv` / `generateEnvDts` / `generateConfigEnv`                                   | `.env` / env type generation.                                    |
| `generateCliOptions` / `flagOf` / `cliFlagOf` / `createCliArgsParser`                    | CLI option generation + parsing.                                 |

## `@deltabox/toolchain/vite`

The Vite+ provider: resolving/running `vp`, the `dbx()` plugin and the `vite`
sync task (see the [Providers](/guide/providers) guide).

| Export                                                             | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `resolveVp(cwd?)` / `hasVp(cwd?)` / `runVp(args, options?)`        | Resolve and run the `vp` binary (local shim, global, then `npx`).                                   |
| `vpVersion(cwd?)` / `describeVp(cwd?)` / `which(bin)`              | Version, resolution description and PATH lookup.                                                    |
| `VP_COMMANDS` / `viteCommandName(name)` / `resolveVpCommand(name)` | The `vp` command catalog + name/alias resolution.                                                   |
| `viteProvider()` / `viteCommands()`                                | The provider descriptor and the `dbx vite:*` commands.                                              |
| `dbx(options?)` / `DBX_TASKS` / `dbxTaskCommand(sub)`              | The Vite/Vite+ plugin and the resolved `run.tasks` to spread in.                                    |
| `resolveDbx(cwd?)` / `runDbx(args, cwd?)`                          | Resolve/run the `dbx` binary (the project's own first; a pinned project never runs a global `dbx`). |
| `resolveVite(options?)`                                            | Resolve `toolchain.vite` (or a passed `toolchain`), with inline `vite` overrides.                   |
| `detectViteSpecifier(cwd)`                                         | Which package (`vite` / `vite-plus`) the project has, for the shim import.                          |
| `renderViteConfig(specifier?)` / `viteConfigObject(config?)`       | The managed `vite.config.ts` shim (per specifier) + the section minus `config`.                     |
| `viteSyncTask()`                                                   | The `vite` sync task that writes the shim.                                                          |
| `resolveFmtCustomGroups(input?)`                                   | Re-exported from core: the `sortImports` workspace group resolver.                                  |

`formatLine(line, repo)` normalizes a changelog line in place: numeric-only
short hashes (eg. `#4033009`) stay commit links, genuine issue numbers stay
issue links, and a bare `BREAKING CHANGE:` marker is bolded unless it is already
bold.

# Registering commands

Packages export framework-agnostic `CliCommand[]` descriptors; build them into a
program with `engine.cli.program.create()` (preferred), or with the lower-level
`createConfigProgram` when the command list is not tied to an engine (this is how
the bundled `dbx` binary and a consumer's own CLI are assembled):

```ts
import { configCommands } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const program = engine.cli.program.create(() => configCommands({ engine }), {
    name: 'myapp',
    version: '1.0.0',
    globalOptions: [{ flags: '--json', description: 'Print JSON.' }],
    disableColors: ({ color }) => color === false,
});
await program.invokeAsync();
```

For config-driven commands, `engine.cli.program.create(...)` builds the program
runtime with schema-derived options and typed `run` values. It accepts the full
program options, including `globalOptions`, `disableColors`, `format`, `argv` and
the output hooks. See
[Running a built program](/guide/config-generator/api#running-a-built-program)
and the
[program members](/guide/config-generator/api#program-members-and-options).

Custom descriptors do not need to be added to `builtinCommands()` to appear in
the generated reference. Pass the same command list to `generateCliDocs`:

```ts
import { builtinCommands } from '@deltabox/toolchain/cli';
import { generateCliDocs } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const markdown = generateCliDocs([...builtinCommands(), ...myCommands], {
    prefix: 'my-cli',
});
```

`generateCliDocs` omits `hidden` commands, keeps the first of any duplicate
name, and renders args/options (with defaults) the same way as the `dbx`
reference.

## Typed command args

`CliCommand` infers its `run(args, context)` object from the literal `options`
list. Use `defineCliCommand` so the literal tuple is preserved:

```ts
import { defineCliCommand } from '@deltabox/toolchain/shared';

const command = defineCliCommand({
    name: 'serve',
    description: 'Serve.',
    options: [
        { flags: '--json', description: 'JSON output.' },
        { flags: '--cwd <dir>', description: 'Project root.' },
        { flags: '--tag <value...>', description: 'Tags.' },
        { flags: '--no-color', description: 'Disable colour.' },
    ],
    // args.json?: boolean, args.cwd?: string,
    // args.tag?: string[], args.color?: boolean
    run: args => serve(args),
});
```

The same inference is available as a type through
`CliOptionValues<typeof options>`. Unknown positional args and dynamic flags
remain addressable through the index signature.

Descriptors also carry optional `argv` and `bin` fields. `argv` feeds the
standalone config program runtime (`program.invoke()`/`invokeAsync()`, defaulting
to `process.argv.slice(2)`); `bin` makes that runtime execute a relative or
absolute binary instead of the in-process `run`. See
[the config program runtime](/guide/config-generator/api#running-a-built-program)
for `create()`, hooks and help/error formatting.

url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/api/subpath-exports.md

# Subpath exports

| Import                          | What it provides                                                                                |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/cli`       | Build the `dbx` engine program + bare-command routing.                                          |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/core`      | Load `dbx.config.*`, run/watch sync, the project graph, manifest, reset.                        |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/config`    | The Zod/env config engine, generators, `config:*` commands and CLI program runtime.             |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/vite`      | Resolve/run `vp`, the Vite+ provider, the `dbx()` plugin and `vite` sync.                       |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/migrate`   | Pluggable migrations to Oxfmt/Oxlint (Biome, ESLint, Prettier, Dprint).                         |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/template`  | The builtin/local/online template registry, loading and scaffolding.                            |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/providers` | The provider registry (`toolchainProviders`) the editor reads.                                  |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/pack`      | The tsdown base config, `createTsdownConfig`, post banner and cleanup.                          |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/tsconfig`  | The tsconfig sync task, templates and the tsconfig generator.                                   |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/changelog` | The changelog runner, workflows, commitlint and the changelog sync task.                        |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/biome`     | The generic Biome config, rendering helpers and the biome sync task.                            |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/project`   | Project/monorepo/workspace file generation and `dbx.config.ts` scaffolding.                     |
| `@deltabox/toolchain/shared`    | The config model, logger, provider model, template engine, ignore defaults, `run`/`spawnCross`. |

# Umbrella (`@deltabox/toolchain`)

The root re-exports `@deltabox/toolchain-core` and `@deltabox/toolchain-shared`
**directly**, and exposes the remaining packages as **namespaces** plus the sync
runner:

```ts
import {
    // identity helper (typed config)
    defineConfig,
    // config + sync
    loadToolchainConfig,
    runSync,
    runWatch,
    defaultSyncTasks,
    // opt-in-by-presence helpers
    sectionEnabled,
    sectionConfig,
    resolveTokens,
    // logging
    logger,
    createLogger,
    // ignore-list defaults
    DEFAULT_IGNORE_PATTERNS,
    DEFAULT_FMT_IGNORE_PATTERNS,
    DEFAULT_LINT_IGNORE_PATTERNS,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain';
// The other packages are namespaced:
import {
    biome,
    changelog,
    config,
    core,
    pack,
    project,
    shared,
    tsconfig,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain';
```

```ts
const { config, tokens, projectType } = await loadToolchainConfig(process.cwd());
await runSync({ tasks: defaultSyncTasks(), cwd: process.cwd(), config, tokens, projectType });
```

url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/contribute.md

# Overview

Feel free to contribute to the development or docs.

> PRs from strangers are disabled for safety and work-load reasons.
>
> Only maintainers are able to create PRs for now.
>
> I only add trusted people as maintainers.
> You can become a maintainer by forking the repo and for a while create your own worthy PRs with bug fixes/features in the forked repo. Only then, you will be eligible to get reviewed for a maintainer role.

## Guides

* [Development](/contribute/development) covers the fork/clone setup, the local
  commands and the linter/formatter bootstrap fix.
* [Documentation](/contribute/documentation) covers writing, previewing and
  building the docs.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/contribute/development.md
---

# Development

## Setup

You need to fork **or** clone this repo:

```sh
gh repo fork deltabox-studio/toolchain # fork
gh repo clone deltabox-studio/toolchain # clone
```

The `dev` branch is the main branch, so no need to switch branches.

## Commands

This repo is a Yarn 4 workspace. Vite+ (`vp`) drives format, lint, test and the
task runner from the root `vite.config.ts`, which dogfoods the `dbx()` plugin.
There is no root `dbx.config.ts`, `vitest.config.ts` or `tsdown.config.ts`.

Node `^22.22.1` or `^24.11.0` is required: that is the floor for the bundled
Vitest 5 and for `vp staged`.

The toolchain config lives in the plugin's `toolchain` option; Vitest and the
published package build live in the standard `test` and `pack` fields.

Each workspace uses a hand-written plugin-mode `vite.config.ts`; Vite and Vitest
resolve workspace imports through `resolve.tsconfigPaths`.

```sh
yarn install        # fresh checkout
yarn dev            # run the CLI from src/ via tsx
yarn typecheck      # packages + root
yarn check          # Oxfmt + Oxlint check (no writes)
yarn check:fix      # same, auto-fixing every workspace + the root
yarn fmt            # `vp fmt`
yarn lint           # `vp lint --fix`
yarn build          # packages + root via `vp run` (root pack config)
yarn test           # builds, then package + root tests
yarn test:clean     # remove leftover emulation temp workspaces
```

> `vp` resolves only at the repo root, so run these from the root. A full
> `yarn build` is only needed for the published `dist`/VSIX: typechecks,
> `vp run`/`fmt`/`lint`/`test`, `yarn dev` and Vitest run from source. The
> emulate suite spawns the built `dist/cli/index.js` and therefore needs a
> build. To run a command against one package, use `vp -C <dir> <command>`
> (`vp -C packages/config test`) rather than `cd`-ing into it.

## Git hooks

The project-owned hooks live in `.vite-hooks`:

* `commit-msg` runs commitlint.
* `pre-commit` runs `vp staged`, which applies the root `staged` config
  (`'*': 'vp check --fix'`) to the staged files.

`yarn install` runs the `postinstall` bootstrap, which calls `vp hooks enable`
to install the generated dispatcher and point `core.hooksPath` at it. Disable
hooks for one clone with `vp hooks disable`, or for one process with
`VP_GIT_HOOKS=0`. The dispatcher and its shims live in the ignored
`.vite-hooks/_` directory; the hook scripts themselves are committed.

The VS Code extension's unit tests run with the root Vitest suite. Its
integration suite launches a real extension host
(`yarn workspace toolchain-vscode test:integration`); CI runs it under Xvfb in
the `vscode-integration` job after `ci`. On Windows it cannot run while VS Code
stable is open.

## Random linter/formatter errors

The root `vite.config.ts` imports the plugin from `@deltabox/toolchain/vite`,
which resolves through the repo's self-link:

```
node_modules/@deltabox/toolchain  ->  .  (repo root)
package.json exports "./vite"     ->  ./dist/vite.js
```

Deleting every `dist/` removes `dist/vite.js`, so loading `vite.config.ts` fails
before Oxc/Vite+ can start. Clearing `.vite-temp` will not help.

**Fix:** rebuild the root `dist` without going through `vp` (which itself needs
the config):

```sh
yarn bootstrap
```

This is the checkout bootstrap already used by `postinstall`. It builds the root
`dist` directly from `scripts/root-pack.ts` using Vite+'s bundled `tsdown`,
bypassing the config-loading cycle.

**Notes:**

* You only need the root `dist/vite.js` for config loading. The root build
  inlines workspace sources, so `packages/*/dist` can stay deleted.
* If you clean all `dist` dirs again, run `yarn bootstrap` (or `yarn install`,
  which re-runs the `postinstall`) before using the Oxc VS Code extension or
  `vp`.

## Docs

The docs live in `apps/docs` (VitePress). See
[Documentation](/contribute/documentation) for the local preview, build and
writing workflow.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/contribute/documentation.md
---

# Documentation

Full documentation, guides and examples live at
[toolchain.deltabox.studio](https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide).

The source pages live in `apps/docs` and are built with VitePress.

## Preview locally

```sh
yarn workspace @deltabox/toolchain-docs dev
```

## Build

```sh
yarn docs build
```

The build also regenerates the LLM bundles (`llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`) and
copies them to the repo root.

## Writing pages

* Add Markdown pages under `apps/docs/guide`, `apps/docs/config` or
  `apps/docs/contribute`.
* The guide sidebar is generated from the docs tree, so a new page appears in
  its section automatically. New top-level sections, the navbar and the manual
  Introduction groups are configured in `apps/docs/.vitepress/config.ts`.
* The pages under `apps/docs/config` are generated. Run `yarn config:generate`
  after changing the config schema; do not edit those pages by hand.
* Run `yarn fmt` and `yarn docs build` before opening a PR.

See the [VitePress documentation](https://vitepress.dev/) for Markdown syntax
and theme options.

## Development

See [Development](/contribute/development) for the repo setup, commands and the
linter/formatter bootstrap fix.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/llms.md
---
# LLMs

This documentation is published in machine-readable forms so LLMs and coding
agents can read it efficiently, following the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org)
standard:

* [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt) — a concise, link-first overview: a short description,
  how the toolchain works, and a table of contents linking to the Markdown
  version of every page. Small enough to fit in a context window.
* [`/llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) — the **entire** documentation concatenated
  into a single Markdown file, for when an agent wants everything in one fetch.

Every page is also available as raw Markdown by appending `.md` to its URL (eg.
`/guide/tsconfig.md`).

## When the site is unavailable

If `https://toolchain.deltabox.studio` is down, the same documentation lives in
the repository at
[github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/tree/main/apps/docs](https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/tree/main/apps/docs).

## 2.6.0 (November 2026)

* Route fmt/lint to the active tool and opt scaffolds into catalogs ([#76df575](https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/commit/76df575) by [T0chi](https://github.com/T0chi))

  * dbx fmt/lint resolve the configured/discovered formatter or linter (oxc > biome > prettier > dprint; oxc > biome > eslint) and run it, falling back to the vp/Oxc passthrough
    * project:init/create scaffolds add the catalogs section for the catalog file they write, so dbx sync owns it instead of leaving the managed file orphaned
    * document the active-tool routing and add the dedicated package catalogs guide

#### Cli

* Sync and watch configless projects with the inherited config ([#346060d](https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/commit/346060d) by [T0chi](https://github.com/T0chi))

  * The command context did not expose the ancestor config path, so dbx sync/watch in a nested project without its own dbx.config.\* warned and did nothing. Pass parentPath through the context and allow both commands when it is set. The VS Code Sync all compensation now works for configless projects, while sync --recursive stays config-bearing-only and is documented as such.

- Document watcher scoping and project identity inheritance ([#074bfcd](https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/commit/074bfcd) by [T0chi](https://github.com/T0chi))

  * Update the VS Code auto-sync section and the project guide to match the implementation: watchers are root-scoped and sync only the changed root; project name/scope/description/type are never inherited. Regenerate llms-full.txt.

#### Tsconfig

* Note that refsAuto requires tsc --build ([#74a25b2](https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/commit/74a25b2) by [T0chi](https://github.com/T0chi))

  * Project references are only followed by tsc --build; tsc -p --noEmit ignores them. Document the refsAuto requirement and why this repo keeps the references hand-written (refsAuto: false).

* Document every generator and generateCliDocs ([#28f812e](https://github.com/deltabox-studio/toolchain/commit/28f812e) by [T0chi](https://github.com/T0chi))
